definition_zh: 资本主义的；带有资本主义特征的；以私人资本盈利为动力的
definition_en: of, relating to, or characteristic of an economic system in which private owners invest capital for profit
core_image: 一间厂房里机器归一个主人所有，开机的人只拿到一张按小时计薪的工牌
scene: 老工业城的街面上，厂房归私人所有，工人按日领薪，市政府只管收税与发照。 The old mill town is often described as a capitalistic economy in miniature.
sceneCN: 这里 capitalistic 指「与私人资本主导的经济制度相关的」（第 1 个义项：属于以私人资本和市场交换为基础的经济制度）；句意为这座老磨坊城常被说成一个缩微的资本主义经济。图中可辨识物件：红砖厂房、私人铭牌、工牌、打卡钟、税务告示。

pos.zh: 资本主义的；具有资本主义特征的

senses.title: Belonging to a private-capital economy
senses.titleCN: 属于私人资本主导的经济制度
senses.definition: belonging to an economic order in which private owners hold the means of production and buy labour for wages
senses.definitionCN: 属于这样一种经济秩序：生产资料由私人所有者掌握，并以工资购买劳动力
senses.example: The old mill town is often described as a capitalistic economy in miniature.
senses.exampleCN: 这座老磨坊城常被说成一个缩微的资本主义经济。
senses.why: The word is built on capital in its medieval sense of a principal sum, so the label points first at the money that starts the enterprise rather than at the people in it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词建立在 capital 的中世纪义「本金」之上，因此标签首先指向启动企业的钱，而不是企业里的人。

senses.title: Driven by profit on invested capital
senses.titleCN: 以投入资本的盈利为动力
senses.definition: organized around the return earned on money that has been put into a business
senses.definitionCN: 围绕投入企业的钱所赚回的收益来组织运作
senses.example: The owners rebuilt the plant only because the capitalistic return looked secure.
senses.exampleCN: 业主重建这座工厂，只因按资本核算的回报看起来稳妥。
senses.why: Capital in this reading is not wealth in general but money advanced in order to come back larger, so the adjective names the motive as much as the system.
senses.whyCN: 这里的资本不是泛指的财富，而是先投出去、再以求更大数额回来的钱，因此这个形容词既指制度，也指动机。

senses.title: Controlled by owners of capital
senses.definition: managed or directed by those who own the machines, land or funds rather than by those who operate them
senses.definitionCN: 由拥有机器、土地或资金的人管理指挥，而非由操作它们的人管理
senses.example: Decisions at the yard remained capitalistic long after the union was formed.
senses.exampleCN: 工会成立很久之后，船厂的决策仍由资本一方掌握。
senses.why: Ownership of the means of production is the defining feature the label picks out, so the adjective also describes who holds the power to decide.
senses.whyCN: 生产资料的所有权是这个标签挑出的决定性特征，因此这个形容词也描述谁握有决定权。

senses.title: Showing the values of competition and accumulation
senses.titleCN: 体现竞争与积累的价值观
senses.definition: displaying the habits of mind that go with a market order, such as rivalry, calculation and the piling up of assets
senses.definitionCN: 表现出与市场秩序相伴的思维习惯，如竞争、算计与资产积累
senses.example: His capitalistic habits showed in the way he priced every favour.
senses.exampleCN: 他连帮人一个忙都要估价，这种习惯带着资本主义色彩。
senses.why: If the system is built on rivals bidding and owners reinvesting, then its habits of mind can be called capitalistic by extension, without naming an institution.
senses.whyCN: 既然这套制度建立在竞价与再投资之上，它的思维习惯也就可以引申地称为资本主义式的，而不必指向某个机构。

senses.title: Favouring capitalism as a system
senses.titleCN: 在立场上支持资本主义
senses.definition: used of an argument, policy or person that commends a private-ownership order
senses.definitionCN: 用于称赞成私人所有权秩序的论点、政策或人
senses.example: The paper took a frankly capitalistic line on the new tax.
senses.exampleCN: 这家报纸对新税公开持亲资本主义的立场。
senses.why: The suffix carries a tone of doctrine as well as description, so a stance can be labelled capitalistic even when no economic detail is given.
senses.whyCN: 这个后缀除了描述，还带有「学派、主张」的语气，因此即便不谈经济细节，一种立场也能被称为资本主义的。

senses.title: Treating capital as the key explanatory factor
senses.titleCN: 把资本视为关键解释因素
senses.definition: used of an analysis that explains events chiefly by the movement and interests of capital
senses.definitionCN: 用于主要用资本的流动与利益来解释事件的分析
senses.example: A capitalistic reading of the migration stresses where the factories went.
senses.exampleCN: 从资本角度解读这次人口迁移，重点在工厂搬去了哪里。
senses.why: When historians or economists single out capital as the driver, the adjective shifts from describing a system to naming a method of explanation.
senses.whyCN: 当史学家或经济学家单把资本挑出来当驱动力时，这个形容词就从描述制度转为命名一种解释方法。

senses.title: Judging success by return on investment
senses.definition: describing a decision or habit that treats profit relative to money invested as the measure of worth
senses.definitionCN: 描述以相对投入资金的利润作为价值尺度的决定或习惯
senses.example: The board's capitalistic test rejected the clinic that served no paying patients.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会那套资本回报的尺子否掉了不接待付费病人的诊所。
senses.why: The medieval sense of capital as a principal sum survives most sharply here: the sum advanced is the yardstick against which everything else is measured.
senses.whyCN: capital「本金」的中世纪义在这里保存得最鲜明：先投出的那笔钱成了衡量一切的尺子。

senses.title: Marked by a wide gap between owners and wage earners
senses.titleCN: 呈现资本所有者与工薪者的明显差距
senses.definition: used, often critically, of a society where the distance between those who own and those who are paid is large
senses.definitionCN: 常用于批评语气，指所有者与领薪者之间差距很大的社会
senses.example: The report called the town capitalistic in the sharpest sense of the word.
senses.exampleCN: 报告用最尖锐的意味称这座城为资本主义的。
senses.why: Once ownership and wage labour are set apart, the gap between them is an obvious consequence, and the adjective can carry that reproach.
senses.whyCN: 一旦所有权与雇佣劳动被分开，两者之间的落差便是显然的后果，这个形容词也就带上了那层责备。

senses.title: Belonging to the capitalist stage in a historical sequence
senses.titleCN: 在历史分期中属于资本主义阶段
senses.definition: used of a period or stage that a historical scheme places after commercial and before later stages
senses.definitionCN: 用于被某种历史分期排在商业阶段之后、更晚阶段之前的时期
senses.example: The chapter treats the factory age as a capitalistic phase of European history.
senses.exampleCN: 这一章把工厂时代当作欧洲史上的资本主义阶段。
senses.why: Historical schemes turned the noun into a stage label, and the adjective inherits that timetable meaning alongside its descriptive one.
senses.whyCN: 历史分期把这个名词变成一个阶段标签，这个形容词便在接受描述义的同时继承了那套时间表含义。

intro.en: Capitalistic joins capital, from Latin capitalis 'of the head, chief', with the Greek-derived suffix -istic. The economic sense of capital grew out of a medieval legal term for a principal sum, and the name for the system was coined in the nineteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: capitalistic 由 capital 加源自希腊语的后缀 -istic 构成；capital 出自拉丁 capitalis「头的、为首的」。资本的经济义从中世纪指「本金」的法律用语发展而来，指称制度的名称则是 19 世纪造出的。年代均为约数。

items.en: Caput, capitis meant 'head'. Capitalis 'of the head' then came to mean 'chief, principal', and this adjective stands at the head of the whole family.
items.cn: caput（属格 capitis）意为「头」。capitalis「头的」后来引申为「首要的、本金的」，这个形容词正是整个词族的源头。

items.en: In medieval legal Latin capitale named the principal sum of a loan as opposed to the interest; the head image survives in the notion of the main sum standing at the head of an account.
items.cn: 中世纪法律拉丁语中 capitale 指贷款本金，与利息相对；「头」的意象仍留在「本金居于账目之首」这一观念里。

items.en: Middle English took capital through Old French in the sense 'principal, chief', and by the sixteenth century it also named money advanced to produce more money.
items.cn: 中古英语经古法语借入 capital，义为「主要的、本金」；到 16 世纪，它也指为再生钱而投出的钱。

items.en: The suffix comes from French -istique, from Greek -istikos, which was itself built from -istes and -ikos; it forms adjectives of manner or doctrine.
items.cn: 这个后缀来自法语 -istique，再上溯希腊语 -istikos，后者由 -istes 与 -ikos 构成；它构成表示方式或学说的形容词。

items.en: The system noun appears in French and German writing in the nineteenth century, and the adjective follows it into English usage.
items.cn: 指称该制度的名词在 19 世纪的法语与德语写作中出现，形容词随后进入英语使用。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and route): no firm first citation is recorded for capitalistic, and whether it was formed in English from capitalist plus -ic or modelled directly on French capitaliste cannot be settled here.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与构成路径）：capitalistic 没有可靠的最早书证，它究竟是在英语中由 capitalist 加 -ic 构成，还是直接仿法语 capitaliste，此处无法定论。

note.en: The first group gathers near-identical forms from the same family plus one distant relative that only looks alike; the second gathers words that describe profit-seeking without naming a system.
note.cn: 第一组是同一词族中形近易混的形式，另加一个只是长得像的远亲；第二组是描述逐利却不指称制度的词。

entries.definition: A noun for a person who owns capital, and an adjective meaning 'of such owners'; capitalistic describes the character of a system or habit, not a person.
entries.definitionCN: 名词指拥有资本的人，形容词指「这类所有者的」；capitalistic 描述制度或习惯的特征，不指人。

entries.definition: The name of the economic order itself; the adjective derived from it answers the question 'of what kind?'
entries.definitionCN: 经济秩序本身的名字；由它派生的形容词回答「属于哪一种」的问题。

entries.definition: The money or assets invested; as an adjective it also means 'chief' and, in older legal use, 'punishable by death'.
entries.definitionCN: 投入的钱或资产；作形容词时还指「首要的」，旧法律用语中指「可判死刑的」。

entries.definition: From capitulum 'a heading, chapter', a diminutive of caput: it shares the head image but means 'to surrender on stated terms', so it is no synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 caput 的指小形式 capitulum「标题、章节」：它共享「头」的意象，却表示「按条款投降」，并非近义。

entries.definition: Says only that an activity is run for profit, without claiming anything about ownership of the means of production.
entries.definitionCN: 只说某项活动以营利为目的，不涉及生产资料归谁所有。

entries.definition: Describes an arrangement in which prices are set by buyers and sellers; narrower than capitalistic, which also covers ownership.
entries.definitionCN: 描述价格由买卖双方决定的安排；比 capitalistic 窄，后者还涵盖所有权。

entries.definition: A neutral everyday phrase for a motive; it makes no claim about a whole economic order.
entries.definitionCN: 中性的日常说法，只讲动机，不对整套经济秩序下判断。

entries.definition: Describes the person who starts and risks a venture; it praises initiative rather than naming an ownership system.
entries.definitionCN: 描述开创并承担风险的人；它称赞进取心，而不命名一种所有权制度。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real family members and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的同族词与真实的固定说法，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Capital traces to Latin caput 'head', and the principal sum sits at the head of the account.
normal.cn: capital 上溯拉丁 caput「头」，本金正居于账目之首。

normal.en: The family runs capital, capitalism, capitalist, capitalistic, capitalistically.
normal.cn: 同族词串成一线：capital、capitalism、capitalist、capitalistic、capitalistically。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the system sense: capitalistic economy, capitalistic system, capitalistic values.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出制度义：资本主义经济、资本主义制度、资本主义价值观。

normal.en: The suffix -istic builds adjectives of manner or doctrine, which is why the word can describe a stance as well as a system.
normal.cn: 后缀 -istic 构成表方式或学说的形容词，因此这个词既可描述制度，也可描述立场。

normal.en: Read it as capital plus ist plus ic and every part carries meaning.
normal.cn: 把它读作 capital 加 ist 加 ic，三部分都有实义。

abstract.en: Picture a workshop where the machines have an owner and the people only have badges.
abstract.cn: 想象一间车间，机器有主人，人只有工牌。

abstract.en: Picture a balance sheet whose top line decides what every lower line may do.
abstract.cn: 想象一张资产负债表，最上面那一行决定下面每一行能怎么做。

abstract.en: Picture a match whose referee is hired by the side that paid for the field.
abstract.cn: 想象一场比赛，裁判由出钱租场地的那一方聘请。

examples.en: The valley's capitalistic farms sell grain to buyers thousands of miles away.
examples.cn: 这片谷地的资本主义农场把粮食卖给数千里之外的买家。

examples.en: Critics call the arrangement capitalistic because the owners carry the risk and take the profit.
examples.cn: 批评者称这种安排为资本主义的，因为所有者承担风险并拿走利润。

examples.en: Textbooks still use the capitalistic model to explain the first factory towns.
examples.cn: 教科书仍用资本主义模型来解释最早的工厂城镇。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「capital（资本）+ istic（…主义的）」——凡事由资本定调 → 资本主义的

root: 拉丁 caput「头」→ capitalis「头的、首要的」→ 中世纪 capitale「本金」→ 英语 capital；加希腊来源后缀 -istic 构成形容词。资本义由「账目之首的本金」引申而来，caput 的更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one line: money is advanced, owners decide, a habit of calculation spreads, the habit becomes a stance, and the stance becomes a stage in a history book.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿一条线展开：钱被投出，所有者作出决定，算计的习惯扩散，习惯变成立场，立场又变成史书里的一个阶段。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mill whose machines belong to one owner while the people who run them are paid by the hour.
core.cn: 核心意象：一间工厂的机器归一个主人，开机的人按小时领薪。

branches.en: PRIVATE OWNERSHIP: the order is named after the owner of the means of production, and its motive is a return on what was advanced.
branches.cn: 私人所有：这套秩序以生产资料的主人命名，动机则是投出之物的回报。

branches.en: CONTROL AND HABIT: owning the machines decides who commands, and rivalry hardens into a habit of mind.
branches.cn: 掌控与习惯：拥有机器决定了谁来指挥，竞争则固化为一种思维习惯。

branches.en: STANCE AND METHOD: the same adjective serves a defender of the order and a scholar who explains events by capital.
branches.cn: 立场与方法：同一个形容词既服务于为秩序辩护的人，也服务于用资本解释事件的学者。

branches.en: MEASUREMENT: worth shrinks to the percentage earned on the sum put in.
branches.cn: 衡量：价值被收窄为投入的钱赚回几个百分点。

branches.en: GAP AND STAGE: the word also names a divided society and a step in a historical timetable.
branches.cn: 差距与阶段：这个词还指一个分裂的社会，以及历史时间表上的一格。

intro.en: The word can be read in three pieces, a Latin noun root, a Greek-derived noun suffix and a Greek-derived adjective suffix, and each piece also builds other English words.
intro.cn: 这个词可以拆成三段：一个拉丁名词词根、一个希腊来源的名词后缀、一个希腊来源的形容词后缀，每一段还构成别的英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin caput and capitalis give capital, captain, decapitate and the whole capital family; the suffix pair -ist and -istic came into English through French from Greek.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 caput 与 capitalis 衍生出 capital、captain、decapitate 与整个 capital 词族；成对的后缀 -ist 与 -istic 经法语从希腊语进入英语。

items.example: The root gave English the idea of a head or a chief.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根给英语带来「头」与「首领」的观念。

items.example: The adjective supplied both the 'chief' and the 'money' senses.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词同时提供了「首要的」与「钱」两义。

items.example: Capital is what is advanced before any return exists.
items.exampleCN: 资本是在任何回报出现之前先投出的东西。

items.meaning: a person, or a follower of a doctrine
items.meaningCN: 从事者，或某种主张的信从者
items.example: The suffix marks either a doer or an adherent.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀或指做事的人，或指信从者。

items.example: The suffix turns the label into the name of a system.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把标签变成制度的名称。

items.meaning: of the manner or doctrine of
items.example: The suffix makes an adjective out of the doctrine.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把学说变成形容词。

items.example: The name of the order arrived in the nineteenth century.
items.exampleCN: 这套秩序的名称在 19 世纪出现。

items.example: The owner of the mill is the capitalist.
items.exampleCN: 磨坊的主人就是资本家。

items.meaning: to turn into capital; to profit from
items.example: The firm capitalized on the shortage.
items.exampleCN: 这家公司借短缺获利。

definition_zh: 体力劳动者；雇工；靠出力换工资的人
definition_en: a person who does physical work, especially for wages and without special training
core_image: 码头跳板上，一个肩扛麻袋的人慢慢走向仓库，掌心全是粗茧
scene: 码头清晨，一排工人扛着麻袋从跳板走向货舱，脚边是散落的谷粒。 A laborer hauled sacks of grain from the barge to the warehouse all morning.
sceneCN: 这里 laborer 指「以体力换工资的劳动者」（第 1 个义项：从事体力劳动并领取工资的人）；句意为一名搬运工整个上午都在把粮袋从驳船扛到仓库。图中可辨识物件：跳板、麻袋、驳船、仓库门、掌心的茧。

pos.zh: 体力劳动者；雇工（美式拼写，英式作 labourer）

senses.title: A person who works with the body for wages
senses.titleCN: 以体力劳动换取工资的人
senses.definition: someone whose work is mainly physical and who is paid for it by another
senses.definitionCN: 主要靠体力干活、并由他人支付报酬的人
senses.example: A laborer hauled sacks of grain from the barge to the warehouse all morning.
senses.exampleCN: 一名搬运工整个上午都在把粮袋从驳船扛到仓库。
senses.why: The root names toil itself rather than a trade, so the person is defined by effort and by being paid for it.
senses.whyCN: 词根命名的是「辛苦劳作」本身而非某门手艺，因此这个人由出力、并由他人付酬来界定。

senses.title: A worker on a site or in a plant
senses.titleCN: 工地或厂区里的体力工人
senses.definition: a worker doing digging, lifting, carrying or cleaning on a building site or in a factory
senses.definitionCN: 在建筑工地或工厂里从事挖掘、搬运、扛抬或清理的工人
senses.example: Fifty laborers cleared the rubble before the crane arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 吊车到场之前，五十名工人清理了瓦砾。
senses.why: The word covers the tasks that need strength and endurance more than training, which is exactly the work found on a site.
senses.whyCN: 这个词涵盖的是更需要力气与耐力、而非专门训练的任务，正是工地上的活。

senses.title: A worker paid by the day
senses.definition: a worker hired for short periods and paid for each day worked
senses.definitionCN: 按短期雇用、按实际出工的天数领钱的人
senses.example: The foreman hired twenty laborers at dawn and paid them at dusk.
senses.exampleCN: 工头天亮时雇了二十名短工，天黑时结清工钱。
senses.why: Day payment is the oldest arrangement for work that needs no contract, and the plain word for toil fits that arrangement.
senses.whyCN: 按日付酬是无需合同的工作最古老的安排，而指称「辛苦劳作」的朴素词正合这种安排。

senses.title: A farmhand
senses.definition: a person hired to do seasonal or general work on a farm
senses.definitionCN: 受雇在农场上做季节性杂活的人
senses.example: Two laborers stayed through the harvest and slept in the barn loft.
senses.exampleCN: 两名帮工一直干到收完庄稼，睡在谷仓的阁楼上。
senses.why: Farm work is the historical home of wage toil, so the generic word settled there first and is still used for it.
senses.whyCN: 农活是雇佣劳作的历史故乡，因此这个泛称最早在那里落定，至今仍用于农活。

senses.title: A worker whose contribution is mainly strength
senses.titleCN: 主要靠力气而非技能的劳动者
senses.definition: used to contrast such a worker with a trained or skilled one
senses.definitionCN: 用于把这类劳动者与受过训练或有专门技术的劳动者相对照
senses.example: The crew split into skilled hands and laborers, and the pay followed that line.
senses.exampleCN: 队伍分成技工与力工，工钱也按这条线分开。
senses.why: The word carries no hint of a craft, so it naturally serves as the unmarked term on the other side of 'skilled'.
senses.whyCN: 这个词不带任何手艺的意味，因此自然充当「有技术」一侧之外的默认说法。

senses.title: Anyone bearing heavy physical toil
senses.titleCN: 承受繁重体力负担的人
senses.definition: used more broadly, and often in writing, of a person under exhausting physical effort
senses.definitionCN: 较宽泛地、常见于书面语，指承受令人疲惫的体力重负的人
senses.example: The poet pictured the laborer bent under a load no machine would lift.
senses.exampleCN: 诗人想象那个劳动者弯着腰，扛着机器也吊不起的重物。
senses.why: Because the root means hardship as much as work, the word can leave the workplace and name the burden itself.
senses.whyCN: 既因词根兼指「艰辛」与「劳作」，这个词就能离开工作场所，直接指称那份重负。

senses.title: The labouring class in older economic writing
senses.titleCN: 旧经济学著作中的劳动者阶级
senses.definition: a collective label used in older political economy for those who live by selling physical effort
senses.definitionCN: 旧政治经济学中用来统称靠出卖体力为生者的集体标签
senses.example: The old tract counted the laborer among the three orders of society.
senses.exampleCN: 那本旧论著把劳动者算作社会三个等级之一。
senses.why: Once the word was generalized, it could stand for a whole order of society, and economic writers used it that way.
senses.whyCN: 这个词一旦被泛化，就能代表整个社会等级，经济学者便如此使用它。

senses.title: Someone who works for another rather than for himself
senses.titleCN: 为他人而非为自己干活的人
senses.definition: used to mark the subordinate side of a working relation
senses.definitionCN: 用以标出劳动关系中处于从属的一方
senses.example: A laborer sells hours; an owner sells what those hours produce.
senses.exampleCN: 劳动者出卖的是钟点，所有者出卖的是那些钟点产出的东西。
senses.why: The absence of ownership in the word's meaning makes it a natural marker of the hired side of a relation.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的含义里没有「所有权」，使它自然成为雇佣关系中被雇一方的标记。

intro.en: Laborer joins Latin labor 'toil, hardship' to the native agent suffix -er. The noun came into English through Anglo-French, and the two spellings laborer and labourer split in the nineteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: laborer 由拉丁 labor「辛劳、艰苦」加英语本族施事后缀 -er 构成。这个名词经盎格鲁-法语进入英语，laborer 与 labourer 两种拼写在 19 世纪分家。年代均为约数。

items.en: Labor, laboris named toil, exertion and hardship rather than a particular craft, which is why the word never narrows to one trade.
items.cn: labor（属格 laboris）指辛劳、出力与艰苦，而非某一门手艺，因此这个词从未收窄到单一工种。

items.en: Source uncertain: the deeper origin of labor is not established. A link to labare 'to totter, give way' has been suggested, picturing toil as a load that makes the body sway, but it remains a hypothesis.
items.cn: 来源不确定：labor 的更早来源未得证明。有人提出它与 labare「摇晃、支撑不住」相关，把辛劳想成压得身体打晃的重负，但这仍只是假说。

items.en: Middle English took the noun through Anglo-French, where labour already meant both the effort and the work done.
items.cn: 中古英语经盎格鲁-法语借入这个名词，那里的 labour 已兼指出力与所干的活。

items.en: The agent suffix -er is native English, from Old English -ere, so laborer is a Latin noun fitted with an English ending.
items.cn: 施事后缀 -er 是英语本族成分，出自古英语 -ere，因此 laborer 是一个拉丁名词套上了英语词尾。

items.en: American usage keeps laborer and labor; British usage keeps labourer and labour, a division that settled in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 美式用法保留 laborer 与 labor，英式用法保留 labourer 与 labour，这一分歧在 19 世纪定型。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the earliest use of the word for a wage earner rather than for any toiling person is not firmly dated, and sources differ by more than a century.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：这个词最早何时专指领工资者而非泛指任何出力的人，没有可靠年代，各家说法相差百余年。

note.en: The first group holds words that look or sound close but mark a different kind of worker; the second holds near synonyms that differ in skill, contract or tone.
note.cn: 第一组是形近或音近、却指另一类劳动者的词；第二组是技能、合同形式或语气上有差别的近义词。

entries.definition: The British spelling of the same noun; nothing in meaning changes.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个名词的英式拼写，含义没有任何变化。

entries.definition: Names the work or the effort, or the verb 'to work'; it does not name a person.
entries.definitionCN: 指劳动或出力，或作动词「干活」；不指人。

entries.definition: From Latin laborare 'to work' in its medieval sense of a place for work, but the modern word means a research room, not a worker.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 laborare「工作」在中世纪指干活之处，但现代词义是研究实验室，不是劳动者。

entries.definition: Built on com- 'together' plus laborare, so it means a fellow worker on a project, not a manual wage earner.
entries.definitionCN: 由 com-「共同」加 laborare 构成，指项目上的合作者，而非体力雇工。

entries.definition: The plain word for anyone who works, including office staff; it says nothing about physical effort.
entries.definitionCN: 指任何工作者的中性词，包括办公室人员；不含体力成分。

entries.definition: A manual worker, usually one with a trade and often male; it implies craft where laborer implies none.
entries.definitionCN: 手工劳动者，通常有手艺且多为男性；它含手艺意味，而 laborer 不含。

entries.definition: Informal for a member of a work crew, as in farm hand or deck hand; it is tied to a particular setting.
entries.definitionCN: 口语中指作业队的一员，如农场帮工、甲板水手；与特定场景绑定。

entries.definition: Defined by being hired, not by the kind of work; a clerk is an employee but not a laborer.
entries.definitionCN: 以受雇界定，而非以工作性质界定；职员是雇员却不是体力劳动者。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real relatives and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的同族词与真实的固定说法，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin labor means toil and hardship, and the English ending -er marks the person who bears it.
normal.cn: 拉丁 labor 意为辛劳与艰苦，英语词尾 -er 标出承担它的人。

normal.en: The family runs labor, laborer, laborious, laboriously.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 labor、laborer、laborious、laboriously。

normal.en: Fixed phrases place the word: day laborer, farm laborer, unskilled laborer.
normal.cn: 固定说法给出位置：按日雇工、农业雇工、非技术体力工。

normal.en: The British spelling doubles the u: labourer.
normal.cn: 英式拼写多一个 u：labourer。

normal.en: Laborer sits opposite skilled in hiring talk, which shows the word carries no craft.
normal.cn: 在招工话语里 laborer 与 skilled 相对，可见这个词不含手艺意味。

abstract.en: Picture a pair of hands as the only tool a person owns.
abstract.cn: 想象一双手就是一个人全部的工具。

abstract.en: Picture a scale where effort sits on one pan and wages on the other.
abstract.cn: 想象一架天平，一头放着力气，一头放着工钱。

abstract.en: Picture a body bent under a load that no crane would be asked to lift.
abstract.cn: 想象一副被重物压弯的身板，那重量不会有人叫吊车去吊。

examples.en: The contractor took on thirty laborers for the summer.
examples.cn: 承包商夏天招了三十名体力工。

examples.en: A laborer on the night shift earns less than the machine operator beside him.
examples.cn: 夜班搬运工挣得比旁边的机器操作工少。

examples.en: The novel follows a farm laborer who never learns to read.
examples.cn: 这部小说写一个始终没学会识字的农业帮工。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「累（lab）的人（-er）」——靠出力换工资 → 体力劳动者

root: 拉丁 labor「辛劳、艰苦」+ 英语本族施事后缀 -er。labor 的更早来源不确定，与 labare「摇晃、支撑不住」的联系仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start from one figure, a person whose strength is for sale, and then move outward: the site, the daily wage, the farm, the missing craft, the burden itself, a class label and finally the hired side of a relation.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一个人物出发——一个把力气拿去卖的人——再向外扩展：工地、日薪、农场、缺失的手艺、重负本身、阶级标签，最后是雇佣关系中被雇的一方。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pair of calloused hands on a gangplank, carrying a load for someone else's account.
core.cn: 核心意象：跳板上的一双粗手，替别人的账目扛着货。

branches.en: EFFORT FOR HIRE: the person is defined by body work first, and then by the place where that work is done.
branches.cn: 以力换酬：这个人先由体力活界定，再由干这活的地点界定。

branches.en: SHORT HIRE: a daily wage and a seasonal farm stint are the two oldest forms of the arrangement.
branches.cn: 短期雇佣：日薪与农场季节工是这种安排最古老的两种形态。

branches.en: NO CRAFT, THEN THE BURDEN: once skill is absent, the word can name the load rather than the job.
branches.cn: 无手艺，进而指重负：一旦技能缺席，这个词便可指负担而非职业。

branches.en: CLASS LABEL: political economy generalized the figure into a whole order of society.
branches.cn: 阶级标签：政治经济学把这一形象泛化为整个社会等级。

branches.en: HIRED SIDE: the last sense is relational, naming whoever works for another's account.
branches.cn: 受雇一方：最后一个义项是关系性的，指为他人账目干活的人。

intro.en: The word is a Latin noun of toil with a native English ending, so the root and the ending each build their own set of English words.
intro.cn: 这个词是一个表辛劳的拉丁名词配上英语本族词尾，因此词根与词尾各自构成一批英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin labor and its verb laborare give labor, laborious, elaborate, collaborate and laboratory; the ending -er marks the person who performs the action.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 labor 及其动词 laborare 衍生 labor、laborious、elaborate、collaborate 与 laboratory；词尾 -er 标出动作的执行者。

items.example: The noun names effort before it names a job.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词先指出力，再指职业。

items.structure: laborare, laboravi, laboratum (Latin verb, first conjugation)
items.example: The verb supplied the international family of labour words.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供了国际通行的 labor 词族。

items.structure: -er (native English agent suffix, from Old English -ere)
items.example: The ending turns an activity into a person.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把一项活动变成一个人。

items.example: His labored breathing worried the nurse.
items.exampleCN: 他吃力的呼吸让护士担心。

items.example: The laborious climb took six hours.
items.exampleCN: 这段费力的攀登花了六小时。

items.example: She laboriously copied each page by hand.
items.exampleCN: 她一页页手抄，十分费力。

items.example: Two teams collaborated on the survey.
items.exampleCN: 两个团队合作完成这项调查。

items.meaning: a place set aside for work
items.example: The laboratory keeps samples at low temperature.
items.exampleCN: 实验室把样本保存在低温下。

latinEntries.structure: laboriosus, laboriosa, laboriosum (adj., first and second declension)

definition_zh: 劳动力；全体员工；在岗人员总数
definition_en: all the people who work in an organization, industry or country, considered as a body
core_image: 厂门口的招工启事与车间里三班倒的人，人事部在册页上清点人数
scene: 厂区门口贴着招工启事，车间三班倒，人事部正在清点在册人数。 The plant's workforce has grown by a third since the new line opened.
sceneCN: 这里 workforce 指「某单位的全部在岗人员」（第 1 个义项：一个组织或地区里工作的全体人员）；句意为新生产线投产以来，这家工厂的员工总数增加了三分之一。图中可辨识物件：招工启事、打卡机、排班表、在册名单、安全帽。

pos.zh: 劳动力；全体员工；劳动力总量（可数或不可数）

senses.title: All the people who work in one organization
senses.titleCN: 一个组织里的全体工作人员
senses.definition: the whole body of people employed by a single firm, plant or institution
senses.definitionCN: 一家公司、工厂或机构雇用的全部人员
senses.example: The plant's workforce has grown by a third since the new line opened.
senses.exampleCN: 新生产线投产以来，这家工厂的员工总数增加了三分之一。
senses.why: Work and force join to mean 'the strength available for work', and an organization's strength is simply the people on its books.
senses.whyCN: work 与 force 组合指「可供工作的力量」，而一个组织的力量就是它名册上的人。

senses.title: The total labour supply of a place
senses.titleCN: 一个地区的劳动力总量
senses.definition: the number of people in a country or region who are available for work
senses.definitionCN: 一个国家或地区里可供使用的工作人数
senses.example: Half the national workforce is now employed in services.
senses.exampleCN: 全国劳动力目前有一半受雇于服务业。
senses.why: Economics needs a single figure for the labour a place can put to use, and the compound supplies exactly that countable body.
senses.whyCN: 经济学需要一个数字表示一个地方能投入的劳动，这个复合词恰好提供了这样一个可清点的整体。

senses.title: The staff a manager can deploy
senses.titleCN: 管理者可调配的员工队伍
senses.definition: the body of employees treated as a resource to be assigned and moved
senses.definitionCN: 被当作可分配、可调动的资源来看待的全体员工
senses.example: The new director reorganized the workforce into three regional teams.
senses.exampleCN: 新主管把员工队伍重组为三个区域团队。
senses.why: The second element of the compound is the same word for physical force, so people are spoken of as a strength to be directed.
senses.whyCN: 复合词的第二部分与「力量」同词，因此人被说成一股可被调遣的力量。

senses.title: The people assigned to one task
senses.definition: the particular group of workers given over to a project or operation
senses.definitionCN: 专门投入某个项目或作业的那一群工作者
senses.example: A workforce of two hundred was assembled for the tunnel.
senses.exampleCN: 为这条隧道集中了两百人的施工队伍。
senses.why: Because the compound names a body rather than an individual, it can be counted for a single undertaking.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词指一个整体而非个人，因此可以按单项工程来计人数。

senses.title: The employed part of the population
senses.definition: those who currently hold paid work, as contrasted with the unemployed
senses.definitionCN: 当前有报酬工作的人，与失业者相对
senses.example: The survey separated the workforce from those who had stopped looking.
senses.exampleCN: 这项调查把在业人口与已停止求职的人分开统计。
senses.why: Statistical use needs a line between people with jobs and people without, and this compound marks the side with jobs.
senses.whyCN: 统计上需要在有工作与没工作的人之间划一条线，这个复合词标记的是有工作的一侧。

senses.title: The collective skills of the staff
senses.titleCN: 员工技术与能力的总和
senses.definition: the sum of what the employees can do, treated as an asset of the firm
senses.definitionCN: 员工能力的总和，被视为公司的一项资产
senses.example: The merger was valued mainly for its experienced workforce.
senses.exampleCN: 这次合并的价值主要在于对方有经验的员工队伍。
senses.why: Once 'force' is read as capacity, the compound can mean capacity in the sense of skill rather than head count.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 force 读作「能力」，这个复合词便可指技能意义上的能力，而不只是人头数。

senses.title: Organized labour in an industry
senses.titleCN: 行业层面的劳动者群体
senses.definition: the workers of a trade or sector viewed as one interest
senses.definitionCN: 把某个行业或部门的工人视为一个整体利益
senses.example: The union speaks for a workforce of nine thousand.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工会代表九千名工人。
senses.why: Collective bargaining requires a single counterpart, so the compound also names workers as an organized body.
senses.whyCN: 集体谈判需要一个单一对手方，因此这个复合词也把工人称作一个有组织的整体。

senses.title: The pool of people who could be drawn into work
senses.titleCN: 可被吸纳进工作的潜在人力
senses.definition: the wider reserve, including those not yet working, from which employers may recruit
senses.definitionCN: 包括尚未工作的人在内的更大储备，雇主可从中招人
senses.example: Childcare costs keep many trained people out of the workforce.
senses.exampleCN: 托育费用使许多受过训练的人无法进入劳动力队伍。
senses.why: When the word is used of what is 'in' or 'out of' it, the reference shifts from those working to all who might work.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词被说成「在」或「不在」其中时，所指便从正在工作的人转向所有可能工作的人。

intro.en: Workforce is a modern English compound, joining the native noun work with force, which came into English from Old French and ultimately from Latin fortis 'strong'. It belongs to the language of management and national accounts. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: workforce 是近代英语复合词，由英语本族名词 work 加 force 构成；force 经古法语进入英语，最终出自拉丁 fortis「强壮」。它属于管理与国民核算的语言。年代均为约数。

items.en: Weorc meant 'work, deed, something made', from a Germanic root shared by German Werk and Dutch werk; it is native, not borrowed.
items.cn: weorc 意为「工作、行为、做成之物」，出自与德语 Werk、荷兰语 werk 同源的日耳曼词根，是英语本族成分，不是借词。

items.en: Fortis meant 'strong'; its noun fortia gave Old French force 'strength, power, violence', which English borrowed.
items.cn: fortis 意为「强壮」；其名词 fortia 演成古法语 force「力量、权力、强力」，英语借入后者。

items.en: The two words were joined in the twentieth century to name the labour available to an employer or a country, a term that belongs to personnel management and national accounting.
items.cn: 两个词在 20 世纪合起来指雇主或国家可用的劳动，这一术语属于人事管理与国民核算。

items.en: Earlier 'force of work' could mean the strength a task demands; the modern sense keeps only the people, and the strength they represent moves into the background.
items.cn: 早期「工作的力量」可指任务所需的气力；现代义只保留人，人所代表的力量退到背景里。

items.en: Labour statistics adopted the compound for the count of people in work, and from there it entered ordinary news language.
items.cn: 劳动统计采用这个复合词来计在业人数，此后它进入日常新闻语言。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the first printed use of the closed compound is not firmly dated, and whether it arose in American personnel writing or in British labour statistics is unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：这个连写复合词最早印行于何时没有可靠年代，它起于美国人事实务写作还是英国劳动统计，亦无定论。

note.en: The first group holds compounds and near forms built on the same two words; the second holds terms for the same people counted a different way.
note.cn: 第一组是用同样两个词构成的复合词与形近形式；第二组是用另一种口径统计同一群人的术语。

entries.definition: The spaced spelling of the same term; modern style guides prefer the closed form for the collective sense.
entries.definitionCN: 同一术语的分写形式；现代体例指南在集合义上更倾向连写。

entries.definition: The building or setting where work happens; it shares the first element but names a location.
entries.definitionCN: 工作发生的场所；共享第一个成分，但指地点。

entries.definition: The amount of work assigned to a person or team; it measures the task, not the staff.
entries.definitionCN: 分配给个人或团队的工作量；衡量任务，不衡量人员。

entries.definition: A desk or machine set up for one worker; it names equipment rather than the body of staff.
entries.definitionCN: 为一名工作者配置的工位或机器；指设备而非员工整体。

entries.definition: The employees of a particular organization taken as a group; it rarely extends to a whole country.
entries.definitionCN: 某一组织的员工整体；很少扩展到整个国家。

entries.definition: The British spelling of the same statistical idea, often including the unemployed who are seeking work.
entries.definitionCN: 同一统计概念的英式拼法，常包含正在求职的失业者。

entries.definition: The people employed by an organization, viewed through hiring and records; it sounds official.
entries.definitionCN: 从招聘与档案角度看的一个组织的受雇者；语气正式。

entries.definition: An older term for the number of people available for work, framed as physical capacity.
entries.definitionCN: 较早的术语，指可用人数，框定为体能式的能力。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real compounds, real relatives and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的复合结构、真实的同族词与真实的固定说法，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Work plus force: the strength a place can put to work is the people on its books.
normal.cn: work 加 force：一个地方能投入工作的力量，就是它名册上的人。

normal.en: The family runs work, worker, workplace, workload, workforce.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 work、worker、workplace、workload、workforce。

normal.en: Fixed phrases place the word: skilled workforce, aging workforce, enter the workforce.
normal.cn: 固定说法给出位置：技术型劳动力、老龄化劳动力、进入职场。

normal.en: Force here is the Latin fortis 'strong', so the second half is about strength, not coercion.
normal.cn: 这里的 force 是拉丁 fortis「强壮」，因此后半讲的是力量，不是强制。

normal.en: The word is a body, so it takes a singular verb: the workforce has grown.
normal.cn: 这个词指一个整体，因此动词用单数：员工总数已经增长。

abstract.en: Picture a reservoir behind a dam, measured in people rather than litres.
abstract.cn: 想象坝后的一座水库，只是它的计量单位是人而不是升。

abstract.en: Picture a shift board where every name is a slot that can be filled.
abstract.cn: 想象一块排班板，每个名字都是可以被填上的格子。

abstract.en: Picture a firm's balance sheet listing skills where money usually goes.
abstract.cn: 想象一张公司资产负债表，在通常写钱的那一栏写着技能。

examples.en: The factory retrained its workforce rather than closing the plant.
examples.cn: 这家工厂选择再培训员工，而不是关厂。

examples.en: An aging workforce changes what products a town can sell.
examples.cn: 劳动力老龄化会改变一座城镇能卖什么产品。

examples.en: Automation cut the workforce by half in five years.
examples.cn: 自动化在五年内把员工人数削减了一半。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「work（工作）+ force（力量）」——一个单位能投入工作的那股力量 → 全体员工、劳动力

root: 英语本族 work（古英语 weorc「工作」）+ force（古法语 force，出自拉丁 fortis「强壮」）。20 世纪合成，指雇主或国家可用的劳动；force 在此取「力量」义而非「强制」义。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with the people on one firm's books and widen step by step: a country's supply, a manager's resource, a project's crew, the employed half of a population, its skills, an organized body and finally the reserve outside the door.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一家公司名册上的人开始，逐级放宽：一个国家的供给、管理者手中的资源、某项目的队伍、人口中的在业部分、这些人的技能、一个有组织的群体，最后是门外那支储备。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gate with a hiring notice on it, and a roster inside counting the people who pass through.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道门，门上贴着招工信，门内一本名册在清点进出的人。

branches.en: FROM ONE FIRM TO ONE COUNTRY: the same body is counted at the scale of an employer and at the scale of a nation.
branches.cn: 由一家到一国：同一个整体既可按雇主规模计，也可按国家规模计。

branches.en: RESOURCE AND CREW: once people are a strength, they can be assigned to a department or to a single job.
branches.cn: 资源与队伍：人一旦成为一股力量，便可被分派到某个部门或某项工程。

branches.en: COUNT AND CAPACITY: statistics count heads, while valuation counts what those heads can do.
branches.cn: 人数与能力：统计数人头，估值则数这些人会做什么。

branches.en: ORGANIZED BODY: bargaining turns the crowd into a single counterpart.
branches.cn: 有组织的整体：谈判把人群变成一个单一对手方。

branches.en: THE RESERVE OUTSIDE: the word also reaches people not yet working, who could still be drawn in.
branches.cn: 门外的储备：这个词也伸向尚未工作、但仍可被吸纳的人。

intro.en: The compound joins a native English noun to a Latin-derived noun, so its two halves belong to different layers of the vocabulary and bring different relatives.
intro.cn: 这个复合词把英语本族名词与拉丁来源名词接在一起，两半分属词汇的不同层次，也带来不同的同族词。

latinIntro.en: Old English weorc gives work, worker, workshop and workload; Latin fortis gives force, forte, effort and reinforce.
latinIntro.cn: 古英语 weorc 衍生 work、worker、workshop 与 workload；拉丁 fortis 衍生 force、forte、effort 与 reinforce。

items.structure: work (native English noun, from Old English weorc)
items.meaningCN: 为达成某事而做的活动
items.example: The first half names the activity itself.
items.exampleCN: 前半部分命名活动本身。

items.structure: force (English noun, from Old French, from Latin fortia)
items.example: The second half names strength rather than compulsion.
items.exampleCN: 后半部分指力量，而非强迫。

items.example: Each worker signs the roster at the gate.
items.exampleCN: 每名工人在门口的名册上签到。

items.example: The workplace has two shifts.
items.exampleCN: 这个工作场所有两个班次。

items.example: The workload doubled after the merger.
items.exampleCN: 合并后工作量翻倍。

items.example: The plan is workable within a year.
items.exampleCN: 这个计划一年内可行。

items.example: Her forceful argument carried the meeting.
items.exampleCN: 她有力的论证使会议倒向她一边。

items.example: Extra staff reinforced the night crew.
items.exampleCN: 额外人手增援了夜班。

definition_zh: 就业；受雇；雇用；工作；用途
definition_en: the state of having paid work, or the act of giving someone work
core_image: 招聘会现场，两列摊位前学生把简历递出去，又收回一份回执
scene: 毕业季的招聘会上，摊位排成两列，学生把简历递过去又收回来。 Stable employment is what most graduates say they want first.
sceneCN: 这里 employment 指「有报酬工作的状态」（第 1 个义项：拥有带薪工作的状态）；句意为多数毕业生说他们最想要的首先是一份稳定的工作。图中可辨识物件：招聘展位、简历、回执单、胸牌、排队线。

pos.zh: 就业；受雇；雇用；工作；用途（不可数，偶作可数）

senses.title: The state of having paid work
senses.definition: the condition of being engaged in work that pays wages or a salary
senses.definitionCN: 处于从事有工资或薪水的工作的状态
senses.example: Stable employment is what most graduates say they want first.
senses.exampleCN: 多数毕业生说他们最想要的首先是一份稳定的工作。
senses.why: The noun of action built on employ first named the act of putting something to use; applied to a person, that act leaves them in a state, and English named the state with the same word.
senses.whyCN: 由 employ 构成的动作名词最初指「把某物投入使用」；用于人之后，这个动作留下一种状态，英语便用同一个词命名这一状态。

senses.title: The act of giving someone work
senses.titleCN: 给某人一份工作的行为
senses.definition: the act of hiring or engaging a person for paid work
senses.definitionCN: 雇用或聘用某人从事有酬工作的行为
senses.example: Employment of local residents was a condition of the grant.
senses.exampleCN: 雇用本地居民是取得这笔资助的条件之一。
senses.why: Because the ending marks the action itself, the word can name the hiring event rather than the resulting state.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个词尾标记动作本身，这个词就可以指雇用这件事，而不只是它造成的状态。

senses.title: The number of people at work
senses.definition: the total count of people who hold jobs, used in official statistics
senses.definitionCN: 持有工作的人的总数，用于官方统计
senses.example: Employment rose in services while manufacturing shed jobs.
senses.exampleCN: 服务业在业人数上升，制造业却在减少岗位。
senses.why: Once the state is counted, the word becomes a figure, and official reporting needs exactly such an aggregate.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这种状态被计数，这个词就变成一个数字，官方报告正需要这样的汇总值。

senses.title: Hiring as a formal act
senses.definition: the formal engagement of staff, often in legal or administrative language
senses.definitionCN: 正式聘用人员，常见于法律或行政语言
senses.example: The rules govern employment of foreign researchers.
senses.exampleCN: 这些规定管的是聘用外籍研究人员。
senses.why: Legal texts need a neutral noun for the transaction rather than for its human result, and this word supplies one.
senses.whyCN: 法律文本需要一个中性的名词指这项交易而非它的结果，这个词正好提供。

senses.title: A particular job held
senses.definition: the specific post or position a person occupies
senses.definitionCN: 一个人所占据的具体职位或岗位
senses.example: He listed three previous employments on the form.
senses.exampleCN: 他在表格上列了三段此前的工作经历。
senses.why: In the countable plural, the word shifts from the general condition to the individual positions that make it up.
senses.whyCN: 在可数复数里，这个词从总体状态转向构成它的一个个具体岗位。

senses.title: The act of putting something to use
senses.definition: the application of a tool, method or fund to a purpose, chiefly in formal writing
senses.definitionCN: 把工具、方法或资金用于某个目的，多见于正式书面语
senses.example: The employment of funds abroad drew criticism.
senses.exampleCN: 把资金投往境外招致了批评。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer: the verb meant to fold something in, and the noun named the using of it before it ever named a job.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的一层：动词本指「把某物折裹进来」，名词在指工作之前先指「使用」。

senses.title: The kind of work a person does
senses.titleCN: 一个人所从事的工作门类
senses.definition: the branch of work someone is engaged in, as in 'employment in teaching'
senses.definitionCN: 某人所从事的工作领域，如「从事教学」
senses.example: Employment in the fishing fleet has fallen for twenty years.
senses.exampleCN: 渔业船队中的就业人数已连续二十年下降。
senses.why: When the word takes a field as its complement, it names the sector a person's work belongs to rather than the contract.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词后接某个领域时，它指的是一个人工作所属的行业，而非合同关系。

senses.title: An opportunity to work
senses.definition: a post open to applicants, treated as something offered
senses.definitionCN: 向求职者开放、被当作可提供之物的岗位
senses.example: The clinic advertised two employments for nurses.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所登出了两个护士岗位。
senses.why: If hiring is an act that can be repeated, each opening becomes a countable thing that can be advertised.
senses.whyCN: 既然聘用是可重复的行为，每个空缺就成了可登广告的可数之物。

intro.en: Employment joins the English verb employ, borrowed through Old French from Latin implicare 'to enfold, involve', to the noun ending -ment, from Latin -mentum. The sense moved from using a thing to using a person's labour. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: employment 由英语动词 employ 加名词词尾 -ment 构成；employ 经古法语来自拉丁 implicare「折裹、牵连」，-ment 出自拉丁 -mentum。词义从「使用一物」转向「使用一个人的劳动」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Plicare meant 'to fold, bend'; with the prefix in- it produced implicare 'to fold in, entangle, involve'.
items.cn: plicare 意为「折叠、弯曲」；加上前缀 in- 便构成 implicare「折进去、缠住、牵连」。

items.en: Old French employer meant 'to use, apply, set to work', a loosening of the Latin sense from 'entangle' to 'put into service'.
items.cn: 古法语 employer 意为「使用、施展、使干活」，把拉丁语「缠住」的意思放宽为「投入使用」。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the fourteenth century, first for using a thing and soon for using a person's time or labour.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪借入这个动词，最初指使用物品，随后便指使用一个人的时间或劳动。

items.en: The ending -ment came from Latin -mentum through French and forms nouns of action or result, which is why the word can mean both the hiring event and the state it produces.
items.cn: 词尾 -ment 经法语来自拉丁 -mentum，构成表示动作或结果的名词，因此这个词既能指雇用事件，也能指它造成的状态。

items.en: Political economy gave the word its aggregate sense, the number of people in work, in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries.
items.cn: 政治经济学在 19 至 20 世纪赋予这个词汇总义，即参加工作的总人数。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the first use of the noun for the state of having a job is not firmly dated, and dictionaries differ on whether it preceded the 'use of a thing' sense in English.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：这个名词最早何时指「有工作的状态」没有可靠年代，各家辞典对它与「使用一物」义孰先孰后亦有分歧。

note.en: The first group holds forms from the same Latin stock that differ only in ending; the second holds words that overlap in meaning but measure something else.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁词干、只在词尾上不同的形式；第二组是含义相交、但衡量对象不同的词。

entries.definition: The person who receives the action; employment is the relation or state, not the person.
entries.definitionCN: 接受动作的那个人；employment 是关系或状态，不是人。

entries.definition: The party that hires; the pair with employee marks the two ends of the relation employment names.
entries.definitionCN: 雇用他人的一方；它与 employee 一起标出 employment 所指关系的两端。

entries.definition: The verb 'to hire or to use'; the noun is what results or what is done.
entries.definitionCN: 动词「雇用、使用」；名词则指其结果或所做的事。

entries.definition: From the same Latin folding image, but it means something folded into a statement, hence an indirect consequence.
entries.definitionCN: 同出那个「折叠」的意象，却指折进一句话里的东西，即间接后果。

entries.definition: The activity itself or a job as a task; it does not formally mark the paid relation that employment does.
entries.definitionCN: 指活动本身或作为任务的工作；不正式标记 employment 所指的有酬关系。

entries.definition: A single paid position, countable and concrete; employment is broader and often uncountable.
entries.definitionCN: 单个有酬岗位，可数而具体；employment 更宽，常不可数。

entries.definition: The kind of work a person does, such as teaching; employment asks whether one is hired, not what one does.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人从事的工作类别，如教学；employment 问的是有无受雇，不是做什么。

entries.definition: The act of taking someone on; it covers only one of the senses employment has.
entries.definitionCN: 招人入职的行为；只覆盖 employment 众多义项中的一个。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real relatives and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的同族词与真实的固定说法，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin plicare 'to fold' plus in- gives the root that reaches English as employ.
normal.cn: 拉丁 plicare「折叠」加 in- 构成这个词根，到英语成为 employ。

normal.en: The pair employer and employee marks the two ends, and employment marks the relation itself.
normal.cn: employer 与 employee 标出两端，employment 标出关系本身。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the statistical sense: employment rate, full employment, employment opportunities.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出统计义：就业率、充分就业、就业机会。

normal.en: The ending -ment builds nouns of action or result, as in government, payment, movement.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ment 构成动作或结果名词，如 government、payment、movement。

normal.en: Employment of funds is the oldest use of the word, and it still appears in formal writing.
normal.cn: 「资金的使用」是这个词最古老的用法，至今仍见于正式书面语。

abstract.en: Picture a rope folded into a knot: the action of folding is the hiring, the knot is the state.
abstract.cn: 想象一根绳被折成结：折的动作是雇用，结是状态。

abstract.en: Picture a form with three blank lines, each one a former post.
abstract.cn: 想象一张有三个空行的表格，每一行都是此前的一个岗位。

abstract.en: Picture a gauge on a wall counting people, not hours.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上一只仪表，数的是人而不是工时。

examples.en: The survey tracks employment by sector every quarter.
examples.cn: 这项调查每季度按行业追踪就业人数。

examples.en: Her employment contract runs for two years.
examples.cn: 她的雇用合同为期两年。

examples.en: Full employment is a target rather than a description.
examples.cn: 充分就业是一个目标而非一种描述。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「employ（雇用）+ ment（名词）」——被雇用所留下的那种状态 → 就业、受雇

root: 拉丁 implicare「折裹、牵连」= in-（向内）+ plicare（折叠）；经古法语 employer「使用、使干活」进入英语，加拉丁来源词尾 -ment 构成名词。与 imply 同出 plicare，但 imply 走「折进话里」一支。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with a state, having paid work, then name the act that creates it, the count of it, the formal transaction, the individual post, the older sense of using a thing, the sector and finally the offer itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一种状态开始——拥有带薪工作——再依次指造成它的行为、对它的人数统计、正式的聘用交易、单个岗位、更古老的「使用一物」义、所在行业，最后是那份邀约本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a contract being folded and handed over, one copy kept by each end of the relation.
core.cn: 核心意象：一份合同被折起交出去，关系两端各存一份。

branches.en: STATE AND ACT: the same noun looks at the relation from the side of the worker and from the side of the hiring.
branches.cn: 状态与行为：同一个名词既从劳动者一侧、也从雇用一侧看这段关系。

branches.en: FIGURE AND FORM: officials count the state, while legal texts name the transaction.
branches.cn: 数字与程式：官员统计这种状态，法律文本则命名这项交易。

branches.en: FROM POST TO TOOL: the countable post is recent, while the use of a fund is the oldest layer.
branches.cn: 从岗位到工具：可数的岗位是晚近义，而资金的使用是最古老的一层。

branches.en: SECTOR: with a field attached, the word names where the work sits rather than the contract.
branches.cn: 行业：一旦接上领域，这个词指工作所在之处，而非合同。

branches.en: OFFER: a repeatable act turns each opening into something that can be advertised.
branches.cn: 邀约：可重复的行为使每个空缺成为可登广告之物。

intro.en: The word is a Latin-derived verb with a Latin-derived noun ending, and both parts also build large English families of their own.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁来源动词加拉丁来源名词词尾，两部分各自还构成庞大的英语词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin plicare and implicare give employ, imply, implicate, explicit and exploit; the ending -mentum gives government, payment and movement.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 plicare 与 implicare 衍生 employ、imply、implicate、explicit 与 exploit；词尾 -mentum 衍生 government、payment 与 movement。

items.structure: implicare, implicavi, implicatum (Latin verb, first conjugation)
items.example: The Latin verb already carried the idea of being caught up in something.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词已带有「被卷进某事」的意思。

items.structure: employ (English verb, from Old French employer)
items.example: Firms employ staff and also employ methods.
items.exampleCN: 公司雇用员工，也使用方法。

items.example: The ending turns the act into a thing named.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把动作变成被命名的东西。

items.meaning: having a job; put to use
items.example: Half the village is employed at the mill.
items.exampleCN: 村里一半人在磨坊上班。

items.example: Training makes the group more employable.
items.exampleCN: 培训使这群人更易被雇用。

items.meaning: the state of having no paid work
items.example: Unemployment rose after the yard closed.
items.exampleCN: 船厂关闭后失业率上升。

items.meaning: to fold something into a statement
items.meaningCN: 把某意折进话里，即暗示
items.example: The letter implies a threat without stating one.
items.exampleCN: 这封信不明说威胁却含威胁之意。

items.example: The rules are explicit about deadlines.
items.exampleCN: 规则对截止期限写得很明确。

items.meaning: to unfold, hence to turn to account
items.example: The company exploited a gap in the law.
items.exampleCN: 这家公司利用了法律的一个空子。

latinEntries.meaning: result or means of an action

definition_en: a person or organization that pays others to work for them
core_image: 车间主任把合同摊在桌上，指了指工资栏与社保栏，让新人签字
scene: 人事经理把合同摊在桌上，指了指工资栏与社保栏，示意新人逐页签字。 The employer must pay wages and social insurance on time.
sceneCN: 这里 employer 指「雇用他人并支付报酬的一方」（第 1 个义项：雇人干活并付酬的个人或机构）；句意为雇主必须按时支付工资与社保。图中可辨识物件：合同、工资栏、社保栏、签字笔、工牌。

senses.title: A person or firm that hires others
senses.titleCN: 雇人干活的个人或公司
senses.definition: the party that engages someone to work in return for wages
senses.definitionCN: 以工资换取他人劳动的一方
senses.example: The employer must pay wages and social insurance on time.
senses.exampleCN: 雇主必须按时支付工资与社保。
senses.why: The agent ending marks the one who performs the hiring, so the word names the side that starts the relation, not the side that receives it.
senses.whyCN: 施事词尾标出执行雇用动作的人，因此这个词命名的是关系的发起方，而非接受方。

senses.title: The organization that pays the payroll
senses.definition: an institution, company or agency as the legal payer of wages
senses.definitionCN: 作为工资法定支付方的机构、公司或机关
senses.example: The university is the largest employer in the county.
senses.exampleCN: 这所大学是本县最大的雇主。
senses.why: Corporations act through people, but law and statistics need a single party to hold responsible, so the word extends from a person to an organization.
senses.whyCN: 公司靠人行事，但法律与统计需要一个可归责的单一主体，于是这个词从人扩展到机构。

senses.title: The party that engages services under a contract
senses.titleCN: 按合同接受服务的一方
senses.definition: in contract language, the party for whom work is done under an agreement
senses.definitionCN: 在合同语言中，依协议接受工作成果的一方
senses.example: The contract names the employer and the contractor separately.
senses.exampleCN: 合同把雇主与承包商分别列明。
senses.why: Contract drafting needs a label for the side that commissions and pays, and this word supplies the general one.
senses.whyCN: 合同起草需要为委托并付款的一方设一个称谓，这个词提供了通用说法。

senses.title: One who keeps servants
senses.definition: an older use for a household head who keeps paid domestic staff
senses.definitionCN: 较早用法，指雇有家仆的户主
senses.example: In the old census, a household was listed under its employer.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧时的人口登记里，一户人家列在其雇主名下。
senses.why: Before factories, the typical hiring relation was domestic service, and the word grew out of that household setting.
senses.whyCN: 在工厂出现之前，典型的雇用关系是家仆，这个词正是从那种家户场景里长出来的。

senses.title: The side that supplies jobs in a labour market
senses.titleCN: 劳动力市场中提供岗位的一方
senses.definition: the side of the market that offers work, as contrasted with those seeking it
senses.definitionCN: 市场上提供工作的一方，与求职者相对
senses.example: Employers and graduates met at a hiring fair.
senses.exampleCN: 雇主与毕业生在招聘会上碰面。
senses.why: Economics frames hiring as an exchange between two sides, and this word marks the side holding the positions.
senses.whyCN: 经济学把雇用看成两方之间的交换，这个词标记的是握有岗位的那一方。

senses.title: The party that advertises and selects
senses.titleCN: 发布招聘并挑选人员的招聘方
senses.definition: the party that posts vacancies, screens applicants and makes offers
senses.definitionCN: 发布空缺、筛选申请者并发出邀约的一方
senses.example: Employers now read cover letters before CVs.
senses.exampleCN: 如今招聘方先读求职信再看简历。
senses.why: Recruitment is a sequence of acts, and the actor at every step is the one doing the hiring, so the same label covers the whole chain.
senses.whyCN: 招聘是一连串动作，每一步的执行者都是雇人的那一方，因此同一个称谓覆盖整条链条。

senses.title: The body legally responsible for wages and contributions
senses.titleCN: 对工资与社保负有法律责任的主体
senses.definition: the entity bound by law to pay wages, taxes and social contributions for its staff
senses.definitionCN: 依法须为其员工支付工资、税费与社保的实体
senses.example: As an employer, the clinic files a return each month.
senses.exampleCN: 作为雇主，这家诊所每月都要申报一次。
senses.why: Labour law attaches duties to a role rather than to a person, so the word becomes a status with obligations.
senses.whyCN: 劳动法把义务挂在角色而非某个具体人身上，因此这个词成为一种附带义务的身份。

senses.title: The party contracting work out
senses.titleCN: 把工作外包出去的发包方
senses.definition: the client that outsources a task and remains answerable for its terms
senses.definitionCN: 把任务外包出去、仍对条款负责的委托方
senses.example: The employer kept control of safety standards even after outsourcing.
senses.exampleCN: 即便外包之后，发包方仍掌握安全标准。
senses.why: Outsourcing splits the work from the payroll without removing responsibility, and the older label follows the responsibility.
senses.whyCN: 外包把工作与工资单分开，却没把责任移走，于是旧有的称谓跟着责任留下。

intro.en: Employer is employ plus the agent ending -er. The verb reached English through Old French from Latin implicare 'to enfold, involve', built on in- and plicare 'to fold'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: employer 是 employ 加施事词尾 -er。这个动词经古法语进入英语，源自拉丁 implicare「折裹、牵连」，由 in- 与 plicare「折叠」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Plicare 'to fold, bend' with the prefix in- made implicare 'to fold in, involve'; the notion of being caught up in something is the seed of 'put to work'.
items.cn: plicare「折叠、弯曲」加前缀 in- 构成 implicare「折进去、牵连」；「被卷进某事」的观念就是「投入使用」义的种子。

items.en: Old French employer meant 'to use, apply, set to work', and the reflex of the Latin verb entered English in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 employer 意为「使用、施展、使干活」，这个拉丁动词的对应形式在 14 世纪进入英语。

items.en: The native ending -er, from Old English -ere, marks the person who performs the action, giving employer beside employee.
items.cn: 英语本族词尾 -er 出自古英语 -ere，标出动作的执行者，于是与 employee 相对形成了 employer。

items.en: Early use centred on the household that kept servants, where the person who paid the wages was literally the head of the house.
items.cn: 早期用法集中在雇有仆役的家户，付工钱的人字面上就是一家之主。

items.en: With factories, the word moved from a household to a firm, and by the nineteenth century it named any party that paid a workforce.
items.cn: 随着工厂出现，这个词从家户转向企业，到 19 世纪便指任何支付员工工资的一方。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the moment when employer shifted from 'one who uses something' to 'one who hires' is not firmly dated, and dictionary estimates differ.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：employer 从「使用某物的人」转为「雇人的人」的确切时点没有可靠年代，各家辞典的估计不一致。

note.en: The first group holds the other endings of the same verb, which are constantly swapped; the second holds labels for the same party seen from another angle.
note.cn: 第一组是同一个动词的其余词尾形式，最易互换；第二组是从另一角度看同一方的称谓。

entries.definition: The person hired; the ending -ee marks the receiver of the action, exactly the reverse of -er.
entries.definitionCN: 被雇用的人；词尾 -ee 标记动作的承受者，正与 -er 相反。

entries.definition: The state or act, not a party; it names what lies between employer and employee.
entries.definitionCN: 指状态或行为，不指当事方；它命名的是雇主与雇员之间的那层关系。

entries.definition: The action that the ending turns into a role; using the verb avoids naming either party.
entries.definitionCN: 词尾把它变成角色的那个动作；用动词便可避开指明任何一方。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning 'able to be hired'; it describes a candidate rather than naming the party that pays.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，意为「可被雇用的」；它描述候选人，而不指付款的一方。

entries.definition: The person in charge of you at work; it is about authority, not about who signs the payroll.
entries.definitionCN: 工作中管你的人；讲的是权威，不是谁签工资单。

entries.definition: Someone who directs staff or operations; a manager may itself be an employee.
entries.definitionCN: 指挥员工或业务的人；管理者本人也可能是雇员。

entries.definition: The party that buys professional services; in contract use it can stand where employer stands for manual work.
entries.definitionCN: 购买专业服务的一方；在合同用语里，体力工作的场合可用它替代 employer。

entries.definition: The firm that takes on the work; it is hired by the employer rather than hiring for it.
entries.definitionCN: 承接工作的公司；它是被雇主雇用，而非替雇主雇人。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real relatives and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的同族词与真实的固定说法，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The ending -er marks the doer, and -ee marks the receiver, so employer and employee face each other.
normal.cn: 词尾 -er 标出施动者，-ee 标出受动者，因此 employer 与 employee 彼此相对。

normal.en: The root is Latin plicare 'to fold', the same stock as imply and explicit.
normal.cn: 词根是拉丁 plicare「折叠」，与 imply、explicit 同出一源。

normal.en: Fixed phrases place the word: large employer, former employer, employer contributions.
normal.cn: 固定说法给出位置：大型雇主、前雇主、雇主缴纳部分。

normal.en: The verb employ supplies employer, employee, employment and employable.
normal.cn: 动词 employ 提供了 employer、employee、employment 与 employable。

normal.en: In law the word is a status with duties, which is why one can be an employer without being anyone's boss.
normal.cn: 在法律上这个词是附带义务的身份，因此可以是不管人的雇主。

abstract.en: Picture one hand passing a contract to another hand, and only one of them keeps the copy.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把合同递给另一只手，只有一方留下副本。

abstract.en: Picture a name printed at the top of a payroll sheet, above every other name.
abstract.cn: 想象工资单最上方印着一个名字，压在所有名字之上。

abstract.en: Picture a door with two handles, one marked hire and one marked hired.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门有两个把手，一个写「雇」，一个写「被雇」。

examples.en: Her former employer wrote her a reference.
examples.cn: 她的前雇主为她写了推荐信。

examples.en: The factory is the town's largest employer.
examples.cn: 这家工厂是镇上最大的雇主。

examples.en: Employers must keep wage records for six years.
examples.cn: 雇主必须保存工资记录六年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「employ（雇用）+ er（的人）」——雇人的那一方 → 雇主

root: employ（拉丁 implicare「折裹」，经古法语 employer）+ 英语本族施事后缀 -er。与 employee 的词尾 -ee 相对；本词指雇用关系的发起方。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start with one person who pays wages, then widen to the firm, the contracting party, the old household head, the market side, the recruiter, the legal status and finally the outsourcer.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一个人开始——付工钱的那个人——再依次扩展到公司、合同当事方、旧时的户主、市场一侧、招聘方、法定身份，最后是发包方。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a contract laid on a table with two signature lines, and the employer is the line that pays.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上摊着一份合同，有两条签字线，雇主是负责付款的那一条。

branches.en: PERSON AND FIRM: the label moves from the individual who hires to the organization that signs the payroll.
branches.cn: 人与公司：这个称谓从雇人的个人移向签工资单的组织。

branches.en: CONTRACT AND HOUSEHOLD: the legal party and the old master of servants are two faces of the same payer.
branches.cn: 合同与家户：法律当事方与旧时家主是同一个付款者的两张面孔。

branches.en: MARKET AND SEARCH: one side holds the posts, and that side also posts and selects.
branches.cn: 市场与招聘：一方握着岗位，这一方也负责发布与挑选。

branches.en: STATUS: law turns the role into a bundle of duties that outlast any single manager.
branches.cn: 身份：法律把这个角色变成一束义务，其存续超过任何一位管理者。

branches.en: OUTSOURCER: responsibility stays with the payer even when the work leaves the building.
branches.cn: 发包方：即便工作离开厂区，责任仍留在付款者身上。

intro.en: The word is one Latin-derived verb with a native agent ending, and either half can be read on its own.
intro.cn: 这个词是一个拉丁来源动词配英语本族施事词尾，两半都可以单独读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin plicare and implicare also give employ, employee, employment, imply, implicate and explicit; the ending -er marks the agent.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 plicare 与 implicare 还衍生 employ、employee、employment、imply、implicate 与 explicit；词尾 -er 标出施事者。

items.structure: employ (English verb, from Old French employer, from Latin implicare)
items.example: The firm employs forty people.
items.exampleCN: 这家公司雇了四十人。

items.structure: -er (native English agent ending, from Old English -ere)
items.example: The ending picks out the party that acts.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾挑出行动的一方。

items.structure: -ee (French past-participle ending used as a suffix)
items.example: The two endings face each other like a mirror.
items.exampleCN: 两个词尾像镜子一样彼此相对。

items.example: Every employee has a badge.
items.exampleCN: 每名雇员都有工牌。

items.meaning: the state or act of being hired
items.example: Employment rose in the service sector.
items.exampleCN: 服务业就业人数上升。

items.example: The course makes graduates more employable.
items.exampleCN: 这门课让毕业生更易被雇用。

items.meaning: to fold someone into a matter
items.example: The letter implicated two officials.
items.exampleCN: 这封信牵涉两名官员。

items.example: The contract is explicit about overtime.
items.exampleCN: 合同对加班写得很明确。

latinEntries.structure: implicatus, implicata, implicatum (participle used as adjective)

definition_zh: 雇员；受雇于人并按劳取酬的劳动者
definition_en: a person who is hired to work for another person or organization in return for wages or a salary
core_image: 一个挂着工牌的人刷卡走进别人的厂房，他的工时被记在别人的账簿上
scene: 清晨的厂门口，一个拿工牌的人刷卡进门，他的工时会被记在别人的账簿上，汽笛一响就得站到自己的机台前。 Every employee at the plant badges in before the whistle sounds.
sceneCN: 这里 employee 指「受雇于他人、以劳动换取工资的人」（第 1 个义项：被雇用并领取报酬的劳动者）；句意为厂里每个雇员在汽笛响前刷卡进厂。图中可辨识物件：工牌、刷卡机、厂门、汽笛。

derivatives.zh: 可雇用的；具备受雇条件的

senses.title: A person hired for pay
senses.definition: a person taken into another's service in return for wages or a salary
senses.definitionCN: 被纳入他人服务之中、以工资或薪金作为回报的人
senses.example: Every employee at the plant badges in before the whistle sounds.
senses.exampleCN: 厂里每个雇员在汽笛响前刷卡进厂。
senses.why: The word is the noun of the person acted upon by the verb employ, so its plainest sense is simply the one who is hired.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是动词 employ 所作用之人的名词形式，因此最朴素的义项就是「被雇用的那个人」。

senses.title: The wage-receiving side of a contract
senses.titleCN: 雇佣合同中的受薪一方
senses.definition: the party to an employment contract who receives pay and owes duties, as opposed to the employer
senses.definitionCN: 雇佣合同中领取报酬并承担义务的一方，与雇主相对
senses.example: The contract binds the employee to six months of notice.
senses.exampleCN: 合同规定雇员须提前六个月通知才能离职。
senses.why: Once hiring becomes a legal relation, the person becomes one side of a bargain, and the -ee ending marks exactly that counterpart role.
senses.whyCN: 一旦雇用成为法律关系，这个人就变成交易的一边，而 -ee 词尾标记的正是这种「相对方」角色。

senses.title: A name on the payroll
senses.definition: a person whose name stands on an organization's payroll and whose pay is drawn from its funds
senses.definitionCN: 名字列在某个组织的薪册上、报酬由该组织经费支出的人
senses.example: The charity lists forty employees and twice as many volunteers.
senses.exampleCN: 这家慈善机构在册雇员四十人，志愿者则是其两倍。
senses.why: In accounting the person is reduced to a line of cost, which is why the word so often appears beside payroll, benefits and turnover.
senses.whyCN: 在会计上，这个人被化约成一行成本，所以这个词常与薪册、福利和流动率连用。

senses.title: A unit of staff
senses.definition: a member of staff counted as a unit of human resource rather than as an individual
senses.definitionCN: 被当作人力资源单位而非个体来计数的在岗人员
senses.example: The plan adds one employee per shift instead of one per task.
senses.exampleCN: 方案是按班次增一名员工，而不是按任务增人。
senses.why: Modern management talks about headcount, and in that idiom an employee is a countable slot, which extends the word from person to unit.
senses.whyCN: 现代管理讲「人头数」，在这套说法里雇员就是一个可数的位置，词义便从人延伸到单位。

senses.title: A long-serving member of the firm
senses.definition: a worker who has stayed with the same employer over many years and is counted as loyal
senses.definitionCN: 在同一雇主处工作多年、被视为忠诚的劳动者
senses.example: The founder's first employee retired after thirty years.
senses.exampleCN: 创始人最早雇的那名员工干了三十年后退休。
senses.why: Because the noun can carry a possessive, as in my employees, it readily picks up a tone of attachment and length of service.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个名词可以带所有格，如「我的员工」，它便容易带上归属与年资的语气。

senses.title: The holder of a post
senses.definition: the person who currently fills a particular post or office within an organization
senses.definitionCN: 在某个组织内目前占据某一职位或岗位的人
senses.example: Each employee of the month receives a small plaque.
senses.exampleCN: 每月评出的那名员工会得到一块小铭牌。
senses.why: A post outlives its holder, so the same noun can name whoever occupies it at the moment, with the person standing for the place.
senses.whyCN: 职位比任职者活得久，所以同一个名词也能指当下占着它的人，人在这里代替了位置。

senses.title: A member of the wage-earning class
senses.titleCN: 靠工资为生的阶层成员
senses.definition: a member of the social class that lives by selling its labour for wages
senses.definitionCN: 靠出卖劳动力换取工资为生的社会阶层成员
senses.example: The novel follows an employee who never sees the ledger he fills.
senses.exampleCN: 小说跟随一名雇员，他填了一辈子账却从未见过那本账。
senses.why: Seen from society rather than from the firm, the hired person becomes a member of a class, and the word turns collective.
senses.whyCN: 从社会而不是从企业来看，被雇用的人就成了一个阶层的成员，这个词也随之带上了集体意味。

senses.title: A person used for another's ends
senses.definition: a person treated as a means to someone else's purpose, echoing the older sense of being used
senses.definitionCN: 被当作实现他人目的的手段的人，呼应「被使用」的旧义
senses.example: In the satire every employee is a tool with a name tag.
senses.exampleCN: 在这部讽刺作品里，每个雇员都是贴着名牌的工具。
senses.why: The verb employ first meant to use a thing, and the person noun keeps a trace of that: to be employed is, literally, to be used.
senses.whyCN: 动词 employ 最初指「使用某物」，这个人称名词仍留着痕迹：被雇用，字面上就是被使用。

intro.en: Employee is a borrowing of French employé, the past participle of employer 'to employ', which descends from Latin implicare 'to enfold, involve'. The French ending -é was later read in English as the suffix -ee. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: employee 借自法语 employé，即 employer「雇用」的过去分词，再上溯拉丁 implicare「卷入、使参与」。法语词尾 -é 后来在英语中被读作后缀 -ee。年代均为约数。

items.en: Plicare meant 'to fold'. Its further origin is reconstructed as an Indo-European root *plek-, a reconstructed form rather than a recorded word.
items.cn: plicare 意为「折叠」。它更早的来源被重构为印欧语词根 *plek-，那是重构形式，并非有记录的实际词。

items.en: In- 'in' plus plicare gave implicare 'to enfold, entangle, involve'; in later Latin it also meant to engage a person in a task.
items.cn: in-「进入」加 plicare 构成 implicare「卷入、缠住、使参与」；晚期拉丁中它也指让人参与某项事务。

items.en: Old French employer 'to use, to engage someone's service' carried the verb into English, where employ first meant to use a thing.
items.cn: 古法语 employer「使用、雇用某人做事」把这个动词带入英语，其中 employ 最初指使用某物。

items.en: The past participle employé named the person who had been engaged; English borrowed it as a noun in the early nineteenth century.
items.cn: 过去分词 employé 指「已被雇用的人」；英语在 19 世纪初把它作为名词借入。

items.en: The French participle ending -é was reinterpreted in English as a suffix -ee marking the person affected by an action, on the model of lessee and payee.
items.cn: 法语过去分词词尾 -é 在英语中被重新理解为表示「受动者」的后缀 -ee，其范例是 lessee 与 payee 这类词。

items.en: Source uncertain (first citation and spelling): early records vary between the accented French form and the anglicized employee, and the exact date of the change cannot be fixed here.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见书证与拼写）：早期记录在带重音符的法语形式与英语化的 employee 之间摇摆，这一转变的确切年代此处无法确定。

note.en: The first group holds forms from the same family whose endings decide who hires and who is hired; the second holds near neighbours that also name someone who works.
note.cn: 第一组是同一词族中词尾决定「谁雇人、谁被雇」的形式；第二组是同样指称劳动者的近邻词。

entries.definition: The party that hires; the -er ending marks the one who acts, whereas -ee marks the one acted upon.
entries.definitionCN: 雇用他人的一方；-er 词尾标记施动者，而 -ee 标记受动者。

entries.definition: The abstract noun for having paid work, and also for the act of using something.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「有薪工作」这一状态的抽象名词，也指「使用某物」的行为。

entries.definition: The verb 'to hire or to use'; employee is its derived person noun, not a tense of the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 动词「雇用」或「使用」；employee 是它派生的人称名词，不是动词的时态形式。

entries.definition: The French participle borrowed unchanged; the accent was later dropped and the spelling settled as employee.
entries.definitionCN: 原样借入的法语分词；后来重音符被去掉，拼写固定为 employee。

entries.definition: Covers the self-employed and the owner who labours too; employee excludes the owner.
entries.definitionCN: 涵盖自雇者以及同样动手干活的所有者；employee 则把所有者排除在外。

entries.definition: Stresses belonging to a body of staff, often in a school or hospital, rather than the wage relation.
entries.definitionCN: 强调属于某个员工群体，多用于学校或医院，而不强调工资关系。

entries.definition: Names a person by the pay received; it is narrower and more economic in tone than employee.
entries.definitionCN: 以所领工资来指称一个人；比 employee 更窄，也更带经济意味。

entries.definition: A person just taken on, or the act of taking on; informal and often temporary in tone.
entries.definitionCN: 刚被雇用的人，或雇用的行为；语气口语化，且常暗示临时性。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real family pairs and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的同族词对与真实的固定说法，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: employ 'to hire or use' plus -ee 'the one acted upon' gives the one who is hired.
normal.cn: employ「雇用、使用」加 -ee「受动者」，得到「被雇用的那个人」。

normal.en: The pair is fixed in meaning: the employer hires, the employee is hired.
normal.cn: 这一对词义固定：employer 雇人，employee 被雇。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: full-time employee, former employee, employee benefits, employee turnover.
normal.cn: 固定说法：全职雇员、前雇员、员工福利、员工流动率。

normal.en: French employé was borrowed whole, and the accent later gave way to the English ending -ee.
normal.cn: 法语 employé 曾被整体借入，后来重音符让位给英语词尾 -ee。

normal.en: The verb still means 'to use', so an employee is literally someone who is used.
normal.cn: 这个动词仍保留「使用」义，所以雇员字面上就是「被使用的人」。

abstract.en: Picture a badge that opens a door it does not own.
abstract.cn: 想象一张工牌，能打开一扇并不属于它的门。

abstract.en: Picture a name written on a schedule that someone else fills in.
abstract.cn: 想象一个名字被写进别人填好的班表。

abstract.en: Picture a pair of hands rented by the hour, with the rest of the person left outside.
abstract.cn: 想象一双按小时出租的手，人的其余部分留在门外。

examples.en: The firm asks every employee to sign the safety sheet before entering the yard.
examples.cn: 公司要求每位员工进场地前签安全告知书。

examples.en: As an employee she could not sit on the board that set her own pay.
examples.cn: 作为雇员，她不能进入决定她薪水的董事会。

examples.en: The survey found that one employee in five had looked for another job.
examples.cn: 调查发现每五名员工中就有一人另找过工作。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「employ（雇用）+ ee（被…的人）」——被雇用的那个人 → 雇员

root: 法语 employé（employer 的过去分词）→ 英语 employee；employer 上溯拉丁 implicare「卷入、使参与」= in- + plicare「折叠」。后缀 -ee 由法语过去分词词尾 -é 在英语中抽象为「被…者」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one relation: a person is taken into another's service, and that relation is then read as a contract, a payroll line, a unit of staff, a length of service, a post, a class and finally a use.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种关系展开：一个人被纳入他人的服务，这种关系再依次被读作合同、薪册上的一行、编制中的一员、一段年资、一个职位、一个阶层，最后是「被使用」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person with a badge enters a plant owned by someone else and is paid by the hour.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个挂着工牌的人走进别人的厂房，按小时领钱。

branches.en: HIRE AND CONTRACT: the person taken on, and the side of the bargain that receives wages and owes duties.
branches.cn: 雇用与合同：被纳入服务的这个人，以及交易中领薪并担义务的一方。

branches.en: RECORD AND RESOURCE: a name on the payroll turns into a countable unit of staff.
branches.cn: 记录与资源：薪册上的一个名字，变成编制里可数的一员。

branches.en: SERVICE AND POST: long attachment and the holding of an office are both read as qualities of the person.
branches.cn: 年资与职位：长期的归属感与占据一个职位，都被读作这个人的属性。

branches.en: CLASS: the same relation seen from society's side becomes a wage-earning class.
branches.cn: 阶层：同一种关系从社会一侧看，就成了靠工资为生的阶层。

branches.en: USE: the oldest layer of the verb survives as the idea of a person being used for another's ends.
branches.cn: 使用：动词最古老的一层留了下来，即一个人被当作实现他人目的的手段。

intro.en: The word can be read in three pieces: a Latin verb root, a Latin prefix, and a suffix that came into English from a French participle ending.
intro.cn: 这个词可拆成三段：一个拉丁动词词根、一个拉丁前缀，以及一个由法语分词词尾进入英语的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin plicare 'to fold' and its compound implicare 'to enfold, involve' supply the verb employ; the suffix -ee reached English through the French past-participle ending -é.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 plicare「折叠」及其复合形式 implicare「卷入、使参与」提供了动词 employ；后缀 -ee 则经法语过去分词词尾 -é 进入英语。

items.example: The prefix directs the folding inward.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「折叠」引向内部。

items.example: The root supplies the image of something folded into a task.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「被折进某项事务」的意象。

items.example: To employ someone is to involve that person in your affairs.
items.exampleCN: 雇用某人就是把他卷入你的事务。

items.structure: employ (English verb from Old French employer)
items.example: The yard employs three hundred hands.
items.exampleCN: 这个场地雇了三百名工人。

items.example: The ending marks the one who receives the action.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾标记承受动作的人。

items.example: The agent suffix marks the one who hires.
items.exampleCN: 施动后缀标记雇人的那一方。

items.example: Employment rose with the new factory.
items.exampleCN: 随着新工厂开工，就业上升。

items.example: Each employee signs the sheet.
items.exampleCN: 每名雇员都要签那份表。

items.example: The course makes the trainees employable.
items.exampleCN: 这门课程让学员具备受雇条件。

definition_zh: 失业；失业状态；失业人数（总称）
definition_en: the state of being without paid work while wanting it, or the amount of such joblessness in a population
core_image: 关停的车间门口贴着一张被雨打湿的招工启事，等活的人站在檐下数着日子
scene: 工厂关门后的第三个季度，车间里只剩下看门的老工人，招工启事贴了又被雨打湿，等活的人站在檐下数日子。 Unemployment in the mill town doubled within a year.
sceneCN: 这里 unemployment 指「有劳动意愿却找不到工作的处境」（第 1 个义项：劳动力想工作而无岗位可做的状态）；句意为这座磨坊城的失业人数在一年内翻了一倍。图中可辨识物件：关停的车间、招工启事、檐下等候的人群、空荡的班表。

pos.zh: 失业；失业状态；失业人数

senses.title: The state of having no work
senses.definition: the condition of being without paid work while able and willing to take it
senses.definitionCN: 有能力也愿意工作，却没有有薪工作的处境
senses.example: Unemployment in the mill town doubled within a year.
senses.exampleCN: 这座磨坊城的失业人数在一年内翻了一倍。
senses.why: The native negative prefix un- simply reverses employment, so the plainest sense is the absence of the state the base noun names.
senses.whyCN: 本族否定前缀 un- 只是把 employment 反过来，因此最朴素的义项就是基础名词所指状态的缺席。

senses.title: The unemployment rate
senses.definition: a percentage expressing the share of the labour force that is without work and seeking it
senses.definitionCN: 表示劳动力中没有工作并正在求职者所占比例的百分数
senses.example: The unemployment rate stayed above eight percent for two years.
senses.exampleCN: 失业率连续两年高于百分之八。
senses.why: Once the state is counted, the noun metonymically names the statistic, so the same word can sit beside rate without change of form.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这种状态被计数，名词便以提喻方式指称那个统计值，因此同一个词可以直接跟 rate 搭配而不变形。

senses.title: The unemployed taken as a body
senses.definition: the mass of people out of work, spoken of as a single social quantity
senses.definitionCN: 把没有工作的人当作一个整体社会数量来谈论
senses.example: Unemployment marched through the town square on the first of May.
senses.exampleCN: 五月一日，失业的人群走过城镇广场。
senses.why: A mass noun can stand for the people themselves, which lets the word act as the subject of political action.
senses.whyCN: 物质名词可以代替人本身，这就使这个词能充当政治行动的主语。

senses.title: Seasonal joblessness
senses.definition: joblessness that recurs at the same time each year because the work itself is seasonal
senses.definitionCN: 因工作本身有季节性而在每年同一时期重复出现的失业
senses.example: Resort towns budget for unemployment every winter.
senses.exampleCN: 度假城镇每年冬天都为失业预留预算。
senses.why: The compound is transparent, so any qualifying adjective can narrow the state to one of its regular causes.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词意义透明，任何限定形容词都能把这种状态收窄到某一种常见的成因。

senses.title: Structural joblessness
senses.definition: joblessness caused by a lasting mismatch between the skills offered and the posts available
senses.definitionCN: 由劳动者技能与现有岗位长期不匹配所造成的失业
senses.example: Automation left structural unemployment in the weaving valleys.
senses.exampleCN: 自动化在织造谷地留下了结构性失业。
senses.why: When the cause lies in the shape of the economy rather than in a downturn, the word takes a modifier that names that shape.
senses.whyCN: 当原因在于经济结构而非一时低迷时，这个词就带上一个指称那种结构的限定语。

senses.title: Cyclical joblessness
senses.definition: joblessness that rises and falls with the recurring swing of the business cycle
senses.definitionCN: 随商业周期的反复摆动而起落的失业
senses.example: Cyclical unemployment fell as orders returned to the shipyards.
senses.exampleCN: 随着订单回到船厂，周期性失业下降了。
senses.why: Because the word can name any segment of the labour market, economists attach cycle words to it to say where the loss came from.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个名词可以指劳动力市场的任一细分，经济学家便给它加上周期词，用来说明损失来自哪里。

senses.title: Hidden joblessness
senses.definition: a condition in which people stay on a payroll but have little or no real work to do
senses.definitionCN: 人们仍留在薪册上、却几乎没有实际工作可做的状况
senses.example: The state farm carried hidden unemployment for a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 这家国有农场把隐性失业背了十年。
senses.why: Statistics count only those seeking work, so the word can be stretched to cover idle people whom the count cannot see.
senses.whyCN: 统计只计正在求职的人，因此这个词可以被拉伸去涵盖统计算不到的空闲人员。

senses.title: Not being employed at all
senses.definition: the bare fact of not holding a job, including when that is a matter of choice
senses.definitionCN: 不持有工作的单纯事实，也包括出于自愿的情形
senses.example: Her unemployment was voluntary and lasted one summer.
senses.exampleCN: 她的不就业是自愿的，只持续了一个夏天。
senses.why: Stripped of the search requirement, un- plus employment simply denies the noun, which is the widest reading of the word.
senses.whyCN: 一旦去掉「正在求职」这一条件，un- 加 employment 就只是否定这个名词，这是这个词最宽的读法。

intro.en: Unemployment joins the native English negative prefix un- to employment, a noun formed on the verb employ, which came through French from Latin implicare 'to enfold, involve'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: unemployment 由英语本族的否定前缀 un- 加 employment 构成；employment 则派生自动词 employ，后者经法语来自拉丁 implicare「卷入、使参与」。年代均为约数。

items.en: The negative prefix un- is native to Old English, with counterparts in German and Dutch; it reverses the meaning of the word it attaches to.
items.cn: 否定前缀 un- 是古英语本族成分，在德语与荷兰语中也有对应形式；它把所附之词的意义反过来。

items.en: Plicare meant 'to fold'; its deeper source is reconstructed as an Indo-European root *plek-, a reconstructed form rather than a recorded word.
items.cn: plicare 意为「折叠」；其更早来源被重构为印欧语词根 *plek-，那是重构形式而非有记录的实际词。
