items.en: In- 'in' plus plicare produced implicare 'to enfold, entangle, involve', which in later Latin also meant to engage a person in work.
items.cn: in-「进入」加 plicare 构成 implicare「卷入、缠住、使参与」，晚期拉丁中也指让人参与工作。

items.en: Old French employer 'to use, to engage' and the noun emploi 'use, employment' supplied the English verb and noun.
items.cn: 古法语 employer「使用、雇用」与名词 emploi「使用、就业」提供了英语的动词与名词。

items.en: English employment is recorded from the sixteenth century, first as the act of using something and later as the state of having paid work.
items.cn: 英语 employment 自 16 世纪有记录，最初指使用某物的行为，后来指拥有有薪工作的状态。

items.en: The word became a social quantity to be counted with the growth of industrial statistics in the late nineteenth century; the first use in that statistical sense is not fixed here, and dates are approximate.
items.cn: 随着 19 世纪后期工业统计的发展，这个词变成可计数的社会数量；它在统计意义上的最早用例此处不作定论，年代均为约数。

note.en: The first group holds words built on the same employ stock that are easily confused; the second holds terms for people outside work and for the state of not working.
note.cn: 第一组是建立在同一 employ 词干上、极易混淆的词；第二组指不在工作中的人以及不工作的状态。

entries.definition: The state of having paid work; unemployment is its negation, so the two sit at opposite ends of one scale.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有有薪工作的状态；unemployment 是它的否定，二者处在同一标尺的两端。

entries.definition: The adjective describing a person without work; the noun unemployment names the condition or the total.
entries.definitionCN: 形容一个人没有工作的形容词；名词 unemployment 则指这种处境或总数。

entries.definition: Work that is below a person's capacity or hours; it is not the same as having no work at all.
entries.definitionCN: 低于个人能力或工时的就业；与完全没有工作并不相同。

entries.definition: The verb 'to hire or to use'; the noun stack is employ, employment, employer, employee, unemployment.
entries.definitionCN: 动词「雇用」或「使用」；其名词系列为 employ、employment、employer、employee、unemployment。

entries.definition: A neutral everyday word for having no job; it lacks the statistical and policy overtones of unemployment.
entries.definitionCN: 中性的日常说法，指没有工作；不带 unemployment 的统计与政策意味。

entries.definition: Inactivity with a hint of reproach; it blames the person, where unemployment usually describes a condition.
entries.definitionCN: 带有责备意味的闲散；它归咎于人，而 unemployment 通常描述一种处境。

entries.definition: The act of dismissing workers for lack of work; it is the event that produces unemployment, not the state.
entries.definitionCN: 因工作不足而辞退工人的行为；它是造成失业的事件，而非状态本身。

entries.definition: British usage for a post that is no longer needed, and for the dismissal that follows; it names the post more than the person.
entries.definitionCN: 英式说法，指不再需要的岗位以及随之而来的辞退；它更多指岗位而非人。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: a real negative prefix, a real family and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的否定前缀、真实的同族词与真实的固定说法，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: un- 'not' plus employment: the state of not being employed.
normal.cn: un-「不」加 employment：不被雇用的状态。

normal.en: The family runs employ, employer, employee, employment, unemployed, unemployment.
normal.cn: 同族词串成一线：employ、employer、employee、employment、unemployed、unemployment。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: unemployment rate, unemployment benefit, mass unemployment, youth unemployment.
normal.cn: 固定说法：失业率、失业救济金、大规模失业、青年失业。

normal.en: The word often appears with a cause adjective: seasonal, structural, cyclical, long-term.
normal.cn: 这个词常与表原因的形容词连用：季节性的、结构性的、周期性的、长期的。

normal.en: Statistics fixed the modern sense: a rate, a total, a policy target.
normal.cn: 统计学固定了现代义：一个比率、一个总数、一个政策目标。

abstract.en: Picture a gate that stays shut while a crowd waits outside with tools in hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门关着，人群拿着工具在外面等。

abstract.en: Picture a line on a chart that climbs while the workshop floor stands empty.
abstract.cn: 想象图表上一条线往上走，车间地面却空着。

abstract.en: Picture a name still on the payroll with no machine left to run.
abstract.cn: 想象名字还留在薪册上，却没有机器可开。

examples.en: Unemployment rose faster in the towns that depended on one factory.
examples.cn: 依赖单一工厂的城镇，失业上升得更快。

examples.en: The government published unemployment figures every quarter.
examples.cn: 政府每季度公布失业数字。

examples.en: Long unemployment erodes skills as well as savings.
examples.cn: 长期失业既耗损积蓄，也磨损技能。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「un（不）+ employment（就业）」——没有就业 → 失业

root: un-（古英语否定前缀）+ employment（employ + -ment）；employ 经古法语 employer 上溯拉丁 implicare「卷入、使参与」= in- + plicare「折叠」，plicare 更深来源为重构形式 *plek-。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gap: the absence of paid work is first a personal state, then a rate, a mass, a seasonal habit, a structural misfit, a cycle, a hidden idleness and finally the bare fact of not holding a job.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一道缺口展开：有薪工作的缺席先是个人的处境，然后是一个比率、一群人、一种季节惯例、一种结构错配、一轮周期、一种隐藏的空闲，最后是不持有工作的单纯事实。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shut gate, a wet notice on the wall, and a crowd with tools waiting for work that is not there.
core.cn: 核心意象：关着的门、墙上被雨打湿的告示，以及拿着工具等候却无活可干的人群。

branches.en: STATE AND RATE: the personal condition is counted, and the count becomes a percentage.
branches.cn: 状态与比率：个人的处境被计数，计数又变成一个百分数。

branches.en: MASS AND SEASON: the jobless become a body in the square, and the same absence returns each winter.
branches.cn: 群体与季节：失业者成为广场上的一群人，而同一道缺席每年冬天重来。

branches.en: STRUCTURE AND CYCLE: the gap can be cut by mismatched skills or by a swing in orders.
branches.cn: 结构与周期：这道缺口可能由技能错配造成，也可能由订单的摆动造成。

branches.en: HIDDEN: idle people on a payroll are the part of the gap that the count cannot see.
branches.cn: 隐藏：薪册上的空闲人员，是统计算不到的那部分缺口。

branches.en: MERE ABSENCE: with the search requirement removed, un- simply denies employment.
branches.cn: 单纯缺席：去掉求职条件后，un- 就只是否定 employment。

intro.en: The word can be read in four pieces: a native negative prefix, a Latin verb root, a Latin prefix and a noun suffix, each of which also builds other English words.
intro.cn: 这个词可拆成四段：一个本族否定前缀、一个拉丁动词词根、一个拉丁前缀与一个名词后缀，每一段还构成别的英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin plicare 'to fold' and implicare 'to involve' give employ and its family; the negative un- is native English, and -ment came into English through French from Latin -mentum.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 plicare「折叠」与 implicare「使参与」衍生出 employ 及其词族；否定前缀 un- 是英语本族成分，-ment 则经法语从拉丁 -mentum 进入英语。

items.example: The prefix turns a state into its absence.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把一种状态变成它的缺席。

items.example: The root carries the image of folding into a task.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根带着「被折进事务」的意象。

items.example: The compound supplied the verb to employ.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合形式提供了动词 employ。

items.structure: employ (English verb from Old French employer)
items.example: The mill employed the whole valley.
items.exampleCN: 这座磨坊雇用了整条谷地的人。

items.example: The suffix turns the verb into a state.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成一种状态。

items.example: Employment in the valley fell after the closure.
items.exampleCN: 关闭之后谷地的就业下降。

items.example: The adjective describes the person, not the total.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述人，而不是总数。

items.example: The noun names the condition and its measure.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词既指处境，也指其度量。

definition_zh: 通货膨胀；充气；膨胀；夸大
definition_en: a sustained rise in the general level of prices, or the act of filling something with air and swelling it
core_image: 市场里的价签一个月换了两回，同样一袋钱能买到的面包越来越少
scene: 战后的集市上，面包的价签一个月换了两回，主妇把钱袋攥得更紧，摊主还在往上改数字。 Prices kept climbing, and the country was warned that inflation would reach double digits.
sceneCN: 这里 inflation 指「一般物价水平持续上涨」（第 1 个义项：整体物价持续上升、货币购买力随之下降）；句意为物价不断攀升，该国被警告通胀将达到两位数。图中可辨识物件：反复改写的价签、面包篮、钱袋、记账板。

pos.zh: 通货膨胀；充气；膨胀；夸大

senses.title: A sustained rise in the price level
senses.definition: a continuing increase in the general level of prices, so that money buys less over time
senses.definitionCN: 整体物价水平持续上升，使同样多的钱随时间买到的东西越来越少
senses.example: Prices kept climbing, and the country was warned that inflation would reach double digits.
senses.exampleCN: 物价不断攀升，该国被警告通胀将达到两位数。
senses.why: The image is a balloon being blown up: the stock of money or the level of prices swells, and the metaphor became the standard economic term in the nineteenth century.
senses.whyCN: 意象是被吹胀的气球：货币量或物价水平鼓起来，这个比喻在 19 世纪成了标准经济术语。

senses.title: The act of filling with air
senses.definition: the act of filling a tyre, balloon or other container with air or gas
senses.definitionCN: 往轮胎、气球或其他容器中注入空气或气体的动作
senses.example: Inflation of the raft took twenty minutes with a hand pump.
senses.exampleCN: 用手动气泵给救生筏充气花了二十分钟。
senses.why: This is the oldest physical sense: the Latin verb meant to blow into something, and the noun simply names that action.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的物理义：拉丁动词意为「吹入某物」，名词只是给这个动作命名。

senses.title: The state of being swollen
senses.definition: the condition of something that has been blown up and now bulges or expands
senses.definitionCN: 某物被充气后鼓起或胀大的状态
senses.example: The doctor noted a slight inflation below the knee.
senses.exampleCN: 医生注意到膝盖下方有轻微肿胀。
senses.why: From the action the noun moves to its result, so inflation can name a bulge in a body or a material.
senses.whyCN: 名词从动作转向结果，因此 inflation 也能指身体或材料上的鼓包。

senses.title: Exaggeration in speech
senses.definition: a swelling of language in which praise, claims or promises are blown up beyond the facts
senses.definitionCN: 语言上的膨胀，即赞美、主张或承诺被吹到超出事实的程度
senses.example: The brochure's claims were pure inflation of a modest trial.
senses.exampleCN: 宣传册里的说法，只是把一次小规模试验大大吹胀。
senses.why: The same balloon image serves rhetoric: words are pumped up until they no longer match the thing described.
senses.whyCN: 同一个气球意象也服务于修辞：词被吹大，直到与所描述之物不再相称。

senses.title: The inflation rate
senses.definition: a percentage expressing the pace at which the general level of prices is rising
senses.definitionCN: 表示整体物价水平上涨速度的百分数
senses.example: The inflation rate fell to three percent after the harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 秋收之后，通胀率降到百分之三。
senses.why: A process noun readily stands for its own measure, which is why the word can be placed directly before rate.
senses.whyCN: 过程名词很容易转指自身的度量，因此这个词可以直接放在 rate 之前。

senses.title: Demand-pull inflation
senses.definition: price rises caused by spending that outruns the supply of goods available
senses.definitionCN: 由支出超过现有商品供给所引起的物价上涨
senses.example: Demand-pull inflation showed up first in building materials.
senses.exampleCN: 需求拉动型通胀最先出现在建筑材料上。
senses.why: When buyers bid more than the stock can answer, the rise is traced to the demand side and named accordingly.
senses.whyCN: 当买方的出价超过存货所能应付的量，上涨就被追溯到需求一侧，并据此命名。

senses.title: Cost-push inflation
senses.definition: price rises caused by higher wages, energy or material costs being passed on to buyers
senses.definitionCN: 由工资、能源或材料成本上升并转嫁给买方所引起的物价上涨
senses.example: Cost-push inflation followed the doubling of fuel prices.
senses.exampleCN: 燃料价格翻倍之后，出现了成本推动型通胀。
senses.why: The same rise can be traced from the producer's costs rather than from the buyer's demand, giving the mirror term.
senses.whyCN: 同样的上涨也可以从生产者的成本而非买方的需求去追溯，于是有了这个镜像说法。

senses.title: Runaway hyperinflation
senses.definition: inflation that accelerates beyond control until the currency ceases to serve as a store of value
senses.definitionCN: 加速到无法控制、直至货币不再能保值的地步的通胀
senses.example: Hyperinflation ended with banknotes carried in wheelbarrows.
senses.exampleCN: 恶性通胀以用独轮车推钞票收场。
senses.why: At the extreme the balloon bursts, and a separate word takes over to mark that the ordinary measure has failed.
senses.whyCN: 到了极端，气球炸开，另有一个词接手，标记常规度量已经失效。

intro.en: Inflation comes from Latin inflatio 'a blowing into, a swelling', built on inflare 'to blow into', from in- 'in' and flare 'to blow'. The economic sense is nineteenth-century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: inflation 来自拉丁 inflatio「吹入、膨胀」，由 inflare「吹入」构成，即 in-「进入」加 flare「吹」。经济义是 19 世纪才有的。年代均为约数。

items.en: Flare meant 'to blow, to breathe out'; it is the source of several English words about blowing and breathing.
items.cn: flare 意为「吹、呼出气」；英语中若干与吹气、呼吸有关的词都源于它。

items.en: In- 'into' plus flare produced inflare 'to blow into, to puff up', used of breath, wind and swollen things.
items.cn: in-「进入」加 flare 构成 inflare「吹入、使鼓起」，用于气息、风与鼓胀之物。

items.en: The noun inflatio named both the act of blowing into something and the swelling that followed.
items.cn: 名词 inflatio 既指吹入某物的动作，也指随之而来的肿胀。

items.en: English inflation is recorded from the seventeenth century in medical and natural-philosophical writing for swelling and the filling of a space with air.
items.cn: 英语 inflation 自 17 世纪见于医学与自然哲学写作，指肿胀以及用空气充满某处。

items.en: The monetary use is generally dated to the nineteenth century, when an excessive issue of money was pictured as blowing the currency up like a balloon.
items.cn: 货币义一般认为是 19 世纪的产物，当时把过量发行货币想象成把通货像气球一样吹胀。

items.en: Source uncertain (first monetary citation): the metaphor is plain, but the earliest printed use in the price sense is disputed and may belong to a later decade, so no firm date is given here.
items.cn: 来源不确定（货币义的最早书证）：比喻本身清楚，但物价义最早的印刷用例有争议，可能晚数十年，此处不给出确定年代。

note.en: The first group holds the opposite process, the verb behind this noun, and one word that only looks similar; the second holds phrases for rising prices of different breadth.
note.cn: 第一组是相反的过程、本名词背后的动词，以及一个只是长得像的词；第二组是范围不同的「物价上涨」说法。

entries.definition: The mirror image: prices fall and the currency gains purchasing power instead of losing it.
entries.definitionCN: 镜像过程：物价下跌，货币购买力上升而非下降。

entries.definition: To fill with air or to push prices up; the noun inflation names the process or its result.
entries.definitionCN: 充气，或把价格推高；名词 inflation 指这个过程或其结果。

entries.definition: Describes forces or pressure that produce inflation; it does not name the rise itself.
entries.definitionCN: 描述造成通胀的力量或压力；它不指上涨本身。

entries.definition: From Latin flectere 'to bend', not flare 'to blow': it means a bend in pitch or a change in word form, and is no relative.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 flectere「弯曲」，而非 flare「吹」：指语调的弯折或词形变化，并非同族。

entries.definition: An everyday phrase for higher prices; it can describe one item, while inflation implies the general level.
entries.definitionCN: 日常说法，指价格上涨；可指单件商品，而 inflation 暗示整体水平。

entries.definition: Names the rise as households feel it through the basket of goods they buy.
entries.definitionCN: 从家庭角度命名上涨，即通过日常购买的一篮子商品感受到的涨价。

entries.definition: A general word for something intensifying; it carries no economic measurement.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指某事物加剧升级；不带经济度量含义。

entries.definition: Growth in size, volume or output; it can accompany inflation but does not mean it.
entries.definitionCN: 指尺寸、体积或产出的扩大；可与通胀同时发生，但并不等于通胀。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: a real Latin root, a real family and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁词根、真实的同族词与真实的固定说法，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: in- 'into' plus flare 'to blow': to blow into something until it swells.
normal.cn: in-「进入」加 flare「吹」：往某物里吹，直到它鼓起来。

normal.en: The family runs inflate, inflation, inflationary, inflator, deflate, deflation.
normal.cn: 同族词串成一线：inflate、inflation、inflationary、inflator、deflate、deflation。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: inflation rate, double-digit inflation, curb inflation, inflation target.
normal.cn: 固定说法：通胀率、两位数通胀、抑制通胀、通胀目标。

normal.en: The balloon image survives: an over-issued currency is a balloon blown too full.
normal.cn: 气球意象仍在：超发的货币就是吹得太满的气球。

normal.en: Do not confuse the root with flectere 'to bend', which gives inflection.
normal.cn: 别把词根与 flectere「弯曲」混淆，后者给出 inflection。

abstract.en: Picture a price tag rewritten while the ink is still wet.
abstract.cn: 想象一张价签，墨迹未干就被改写。

abstract.en: Picture a balloon that keeps filling until the skin is thin and shiny.
abstract.cn: 想象一只气球不断充气，表皮变得又薄又亮。

abstract.en: Picture a purse that stays the same size while the bread inside it shrinks.
abstract.cn: 想象钱袋大小不变，里面的面包却越变越小。

examples.en: Central banks raise rates when inflation refuses to fall.
examples.cn: 当通胀迟迟不降时，央行会加息。

examples.en: Household surveys show that inflation is felt most sharply in food prices.
examples.cn: 家庭调查显示，通胀在食品价格上感受最尖锐。

examples.en: The report blamed wage inflation for the rise in service costs.
examples.cn: 报告把服务成本上升归因于工资推动的物价上涨。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「in（向内）+ flat（气）+ ion」——往里面打气，越打越鼓 → 膨胀、通胀

root: 拉丁 inflare「吹入、使鼓起」= in-「进入」+ flare「吹」→ 名词 inflatio「吹入、肿胀」→ 英语 inflation；经济义为 19 世纪比喻用法，最早书证存疑。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gesture: air is blown into something, it swells, and the same swelling is then applied to prices, to a measured rate, to demand, to costs and finally to a runaway spiral.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：把气吹入某物，它鼓起来；同一个「鼓起」再依次用于物价、一个测得的比率、需求、成本，最后是失控的螺旋。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a balloon blown fuller and fuller while the same purse buys less bread.
core.cn: 核心意象：气球越吹越满，同一个钱袋买到的面包却越来越少。

branches.en: PRICE AND RATE: the swollen level of prices is then expressed as a percentage.
branches.cn: 物价与比率：鼓起的物价水平随后被表示为一个百分数。

branches.en: AIR AND BODY: the physical act of blowing fills a thing, and the thing bulges.
branches.cn: 气与物体：吹入的物理动作把东西充满，东西便鼓起。

branches.en: LANGUAGE: the same swelling shows up in speech as exaggeration and self-praise.
branches.cn: 语言：同一种「鼓起」在言语中表现为夸大与自夸。

branches.en: DEMAND AND COST: prices can be pushed from the buyer's side or pulled from the producer's side.
branches.cn: 需求与成本：物价可由买方一侧推起，也可由生产者一侧拉起。

branches.en: RUNAWAY: at the extreme the balloon bursts into hyperinflation.
branches.cn: 失控：到了极端，气球炸成恶性通胀。

intro.en: The word is a Latin prefix, a Latin verb root and a Latin noun suffix; each piece also builds other English words, and the family has a mirror image in de-.
intro.cn: 这个词由一个拉丁前缀、一个拉丁动词词根与一个拉丁名词后缀构成；每一段还构成别的英语词，整个词族还有一个以 de- 开头的镜像形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin flare 'to blow' gives inflate, inflation, deflate, deflation and flatus; in- and de- set the two directions of the same image.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 flare「吹」衍生出 inflate、inflation、deflate、deflation 与 flatus；in- 与 de- 标出同一意象的两个方向。

items.example: The prefix points the blowing inward.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「吹」指向内部。

items.example: The root carries the idea of moving air.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根带着「推动空气」的意思。

items.meaning: to blow into; to puff up
items.example: The compound names both the act and its swelling result.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合形式既指动作，也指其鼓胀的结果。

items.example: The Latin noun supplied the English word directly.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词直接提供了英语词。

items.example: The suffix turns the verb into a process noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成过程名词。

items.meaning: to fill with air; to raise prices
items.example: Dealers inflate prices before a sale.
items.exampleCN: 商家会在促销前抬高价格。

items.meaning: to let air out; to lower prices
items.example: The mirror verb was formed by swapping the prefix.
items.exampleCN: 这个镜像动词是靠替换前缀造出的。

items.example: The adjective describes pressure, not the rise itself.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述压力，而非上涨本身。

definition_zh: 通货紧缩；放气；泄气；削减；风蚀
definition_en: a sustained fall in the general level of prices, or the act of letting air out of something
core_image: 渔村的鱼价一月比一月低，摊主把价签往下改，欠的债却一分没少
scene: 海边的渔村在萧条里过了两年，鱼价一月比一月低，摊主把价签往下改，欠的债却一分没少。 Shops cut prices again and again, and the town slid into deflation.
sceneCN: 这里 deflation 指「一般物价水平持续下跌」（第 1 个义项：整体物价持续走低、货币购买力上升）；句意为店铺一再降价，小镇滑入通缩。图中可辨识物件：下调的价签、空鱼筐、账本、紧闭的店门。

pos.zh: 通货紧缩；放气；泄气；风蚀

senses.title: A sustained fall in the price level
senses.definition: a continuing decrease in the general level of prices, so that money gains purchasing power over time
senses.definitionCN: 整体物价水平持续下降，使同样多的钱随时间买到更多东西
senses.example: Shops cut prices again and again, and the town slid into deflation.
senses.exampleCN: 店铺一再降价，小镇滑入通缩。
senses.why: The word is the mirror of inflation: the same balloon image is reversed, so the currency is pictured as being let down rather than blown up.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 inflation 的镜像：同一个气球意象被反过来，通货被想象成放气而不是吹胀。

senses.title: The act of letting air out
senses.definition: the act of releasing air or gas from a tyre, balloon or other inflated object
senses.definitionCN: 把空气或气体从轮胎、气球或其他充气物中放出的动作
senses.example: Deflation of the damaged tyre took only a moment.
senses.exampleCN: 给受损轮胎放气只用了一会儿。
senses.why: This is the literal sense of the Latin verb: de- 'down, away' plus flare 'to blow' means to blow away or let the air out.
senses.whyCN: 这是拉丁动词的字面义：de-「向下、离开」加 flare「吹」，意为吹走或放掉气。

senses.title: A loss of confidence
senses.definition: a state of lowered spirits after a setback, as if the person had been emptied of air
senses.definitionCN: 受挫之后情绪低落的状态，仿佛人被抽空了气
senses.example: The defeat left a quiet deflation in the dressing room.
senses.exampleCN: 这场失利在更衣室里留下一种无声的泄气。
senses.why: The physical emptying of a balloon supplies a ready metaphor for morale, which the noun can carry without any economic content.
senses.whyCN: 把气球放空这一物理动作，为士气提供了现成的比喻，名词因此可以完全不带经济内容。

senses.title: A cut in scale or spending
senses.definition: a deliberate reduction in the size, cost or activity of something
senses.definitionCN: 有意缩减某事物的规模、成本或活动量
senses.example: The deflation of the program removed two of its four offices.
senses.exampleCN: 该项目缩减后，四个办事处关掉了两个。
senses.why: If blowing in expands a thing, letting air out contracts it, so the noun naturally serves any plan of shrinking.
senses.whyCN: 既然吹入使事物膨胀，放气就使它收缩，因此这个名词自然可用于任何缩减方案。

senses.title: Wind erosion of the land
senses.titleCN: 风把地表颗粒吹走的风蚀
senses.definition: the removal of loose soil or sand by wind, a geological process named after the blowing away of particles
senses.definitionCN: 风把松散土壤或沙粒吹走的地质过程，因颗粒被吹走而得名
senses.example: Deflation has stripped the dune field down to bare rock.
senses.exampleCN: 风蚀已把这片沙丘地剥到只剩裸岩。
senses.why: Geologists took the literal 'blow away' sense and applied it to wind lifting loose material off the surface.
senses.whyCN: 地质学家取了字面的「吹走」义，用来指风把松散物质从地表抬走。

senses.title: A policy of tightening
senses.definition: a government or central-bank policy that reduces demand, credit or public spending
senses.definitionCN: 政府或央行压低需求、信贷或公共开支的政策
senses.example: The deflation of credit came before the fall in output.
senses.exampleCN: 信贷的紧缩先于产出的下降。
senses.why: Policy language borrows the noun because the aim is to take air out of an overheated economy.
senses.whyCN: 政策话语借用这个名词，因为目的正是给过热的经济放掉一些气。

senses.title: Debt deflation
senses.titleCN: 物价下跌加重债务的债务紧缩
senses.definition: the process in which falling prices make existing debts heavier in real terms and force further cuts
senses.definitionCN: 物价下跌使既有债务按实值变重、并迫使进一步缩减的过程
senses.example: Debt deflation turned the slowdown into a long stagnation.
senses.exampleCN: 债务紧缩把放缓拖成了长期停滞。
senses.why: When the measure of value itself shrinks, every fixed debt grows relative to it, and the word names that self-feeding loop.
senses.whyCN: 当价值尺度本身缩小时，每一笔固定债务相对它就变重，这个词命名的正是这种自我喂养的循环。

senses.title: The deflation rate
senses.definition: a percentage expressing the pace at which the general price level is falling
senses.definitionCN: 表示整体物价水平下降速度的百分数
senses.example: The deflation rate eased to one percent in the spring.
senses.exampleCN: 通缩率在春季放缓至百分之一。
senses.why: As with inflation, the process noun comes to stand for its own measurement, so it can be attached directly to rate.
senses.whyCN: 与 inflation 一样，过程名词转指自身的度量，因此可以直接与 rate 搭配。

intro.en: Deflation is built on Latin deflare 'to blow away', from de- 'down, away' and flare 'to blow'; the economic sense was formed as the counterpart of inflation in the nineteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: deflation 建立在拉丁 deflare「吹走」之上，即 de-「向下、离开」加 flare「吹」；经济义是 19 世纪作为 inflation 的对立面而形成的。年代均为约数。

items.en: Flare meant 'to blow, to breathe out', the source of a small family of English words about blowing.
items.cn: flare 意为「吹、呼出气」，是英语中一小族「吹气」词的来源。

items.en: De- 'down, away' plus flare gave deflare 'to blow away, to blow off', used of wind and of emptying something by blowing.
items.cn: de-「向下、离开」加 flare 构成 deflare「吹走、吹掉」，用于风，也指吹气把某物腾空。

items.en: The English verb deflate appeared in the nineteenth century for letting air or gas out of a balloon, tyre or cavity.
items.cn: 英语动词 deflate 于 19 世纪出现，指把空气或气体从气球、轮胎或腔体中放出。

items.en: The economic noun is generally dated to the nineteenth century and was consciously coined as the opposite of inflation, reversing the same balloon image.
items.cn: 经济义名词一般认为是 19 世纪的产物，并被有意造作 inflation 的反面，把同一个气球意象反转过来。

items.en: Nineteenth-century geology applied the literal 'blowing away' sense to wind stripping loose sand and soil from the surface.
items.cn: 19 世纪的地质学把字面的「吹走」义用于风把松散沙土从地表剥走。

items.en: Because the word was built by analogy rather than inherited, its first economic use is generally placed in the nineteenth century, though the precise decade is not fixed here.
items.cn: 由于这个词是按类比而非继承造出的，其最早经济用例一般被认为在 19 世纪，确切年代此处不作定论。

note.en: The first group holds the mirror process, the verb behind it, and one look-alike with a different job; the second holds declines of prices, of inflation and of output.
note.cn: 第一组是镜像过程、其背后的动词，以及一个外形相近但作用不同的词；第二组是物价下降、通胀放慢与产出下降。

entries.definition: Prices rise and money loses purchasing power; deflation is the same mechanism running backwards.
entries.definitionCN: 物价上涨、货币购买力下降；deflation 是同一机制反向运行。

entries.definition: To let air out or to lower prices; the noun deflation names the process or its result.
entries.definitionCN: 放气或压低价格；名词 deflation 指过程或结果。

entries.definition: Describes pressure that pushes prices down; it names the force, not the decline.
entries.definitionCN: 描述把物价往下压的力量；它指力量而非下跌本身。

entries.definition: In statistics, a deflator is a price index used to strip inflation out of nominal figures; it is a tool, not a process.
entries.definitionCN: 在统计中，deflator 是用来从名义数字里剔除物价变动影响的指数；它是工具，不是过程。

entries.definition: An everyday phrase for falling prices; it may describe one good, whereas deflation means the general level.
entries.definitionCN: 日常说法，指价格下跌；可指单一商品，而 deflation 指整体水平。

entries.definition: A slowing of inflation while prices are still rising; unlike deflation, the level does not fall.
entries.definitionCN: 物价仍在上涨、只是涨幅放缓；与 deflation 不同，水平并未下降。

entries.definition: A deep and long slump in output and employment; deflation may accompany it but is a separate price phenomenon.
entries.definitionCN: 产出与就业的深重长期低迷；通缩可与之并存，但属于独立的价格现象。

entries.definition: A policy of cutting public spending; it is a chosen response, not a movement of prices.
entries.definitionCN: 削减公共开支的政策；它是主动选择的对策，不是价格运动。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: a real Latin prefix and root, a real family and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁前缀与词根、真实的同族词与真实的固定说法，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: de- 'down, away' plus flare 'to blow': to blow the air out.
normal.cn: de-「向下、离开」加 flare「吹」：把气吹走。

normal.en: The family runs deflate, deflation, deflationary, deflator, inflate, inflation.
normal.cn: 同族词串成一线：deflate、deflation、deflationary、deflator、inflate、inflation。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: price deflation, deflationary pressure, debt deflation, deflation spiral.
normal.cn: 固定说法：物价下跌、通缩压力、债务紧缩、通缩螺旋。

normal.en: Remember the pair by the prefix: in- blows up, de- lets out.
normal.cn: 用前缀记这一对：in- 往里吹，de- 往外放。

normal.en: Geology uses the literal sense: wind blowing loose sand away.
normal.cn: 地质学用字面义：风把松散沙粒吹走。

abstract.en: Picture a balloon slowly losing its shape against a wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一只气球贴着墙慢慢瘪下去。

abstract.en: Picture a price tag being crossed out and rewritten lower, twice in a month.
abstract.cn: 想象一张价签被划掉、改低，一个月里改了两次。

abstract.en: Picture a debt that grows heavier while the shop's takings shrink.
abstract.cn: 想象店里的进账越来越薄，欠的债却越来越重。

examples.en: Deflation punishes borrowers because their debts stay fixed while incomes fall.
examples.cn: 通缩惩罚借款人，因为收入下降而债务不变。

examples.en: The central bank denied that the economy was entering deflation.
examples.cn: 央行否认经济正进入通缩。

examples.en: Wind deflation has left a shallow basin in the plateau.
examples.cn: 风蚀在高原上留下一个浅盆地。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「de（向下）+ flat（气）+ ion」——把气往下放掉，越放越瘪 → 放气、通缩

root: 拉丁 deflare「吹走」= de-「向下、离开」+ flare「吹」→ 英语 deflate / deflation；经济义为 19 世纪按 inflation 反向类比造出，确切年代不作定论；地质义亦出自字面「吹走」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one reversed gesture: air is let out, the thing slackens, and the same slackening is applied to prices, to morale, to a budget, to the land, to credit and finally to a spiral of debt.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个反向动作展开：把气放掉，物体瘪下去；同一种「瘪下去」再依次用于物价、士气、预算、土地、信贷，最后是债务的螺旋。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a balloon going slack, a price tag rewritten lower, and a debt that does not shrink with it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只瘪下去的气球、一张改低的价签，以及一笔并不随之缩小的债。

branches.en: PRICE AND RATE: the falling level of prices is measured and reported as a percentage.
branches.cn: 物价与比率：下跌的物价水平被度量并报告为一个百分数。

branches.en: AIR AND SPIRIT: letting air out of a thing mirrors the emptying of confidence.
branches.cn: 气与心气：把物体放空，正映照着信心的被抽空。

branches.en: SCALE: the same release becomes a deliberate cut in size or spending.
branches.cn: 规模：同一种「放掉」变成对规模或开支的有意削减。

branches.en: LAND: wind literally blows the loose surface away.
branches.cn: 土地：风把松散的地表真的吹走。

branches.en: CREDIT AND DEBT: tightening policy meets the loop in which cheaper money makes fixed debt heavier.
branches.cn: 信贷与债务：紧缩政策遇上「钱变便宜反而使固定债务变重」的循环。

intro.en: The word is a Latin prefix, a Latin verb root and a noun suffix; the same three pieces build its mirror image and a whole small family.
intro.cn: 这个词由一个拉丁前缀、一个拉丁动词词根与一个名词后缀构成；这三段也构成它的镜像词与整个小词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin flare 'to blow' gives deflate, deflation, deflator, inflate, inflation and flatus; de- and in- mark the two opposite directions.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 flare「吹」衍生出 deflate、deflation、deflator、inflate、inflation 与 flatus；de- 与 in- 标出两个相反方向。

items.example: The prefix points the blowing outward.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「吹」指向外。

items.example: The root supplies the image of moving air.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供推动空气的意象。

items.meaning: to blow away; to blow out
items.example: The compound names emptying by blowing.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合形式指用吹气腾空。

items.example: The Latin noun underlies the English form.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词是英语形式的基础。

items.example: The suffix turns the verb into a process noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成过程名词。

items.meaning: to let air out; to lower prices
items.example: The verb appeared in the nineteenth century.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词于 19 世纪出现。

items.example: The adjective names the pressure, not the fall.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词指压力，而非下跌。

items.meaning: a price index; a device for letting air out
items.example: The deflator strips price change from nominal output.
items.exampleCN: 平减指数从名义产出中剔除了价格变动。

definition_zh: 经济衰退；后退；退离；凹陷；消退
definition_en: a period in which economic activity contracts, or the act of moving back from a former position
core_image: 船坞停了一半，工人把工具收进木箱，酒吧的灯熄得比往年早
scene: 镇上的船坞停了一半，工人把工具收进木箱，酒吧的灯也熄得比往年早，招工栏上的纸被风吹得翻卷。 The harbour town slipped into recession when the orders stopped coming.
sceneCN: 这里 recession 指「经济活动连续收缩的一段时期」（第 1 个义项：产出、就业与交易普遍下滑的阶段）；句意为订单一断，这座港口小镇便滑入衰退。图中可辨识物件：半停的船坞、收起的工具、早熄的店灯、翻卷的招工纸。

pos.zh: 经济衰退；后退；退离；凹陷；消退

senses.title: A period of contracting activity
senses.titleCN: 经济活动收缩的一段时期
senses.definition: a phase in which output, employment and trade fall across an economy for long enough to be measured
senses.definitionCN: 整个经济体的产出、就业与贸易下滑，且持续到足以被计量的阶段
senses.example: The harbour town slipped into recession when the orders stopped coming.
senses.exampleCN: 订单一断，这座港口小镇便滑入衰退。
senses.why: The word keeps its literal image of something moving backwards: the economy is pictured as stepping back from where it stood.
senses.whyCN: 这个词保留了「向后移动」的字面意象：经济被想象成从原来的位置倒退一步。

senses.title: The act of moving back
senses.definition: the movement of a person, line or object back from a position it had reached
senses.definitionCN: 人、阵线或物体从已达到的位置向后退回的动作
senses.example: The recession of the tide left the boats tilted on the mud.
senses.exampleCN: 潮水退去，船搁在泥地上歪着。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: re- 'back' plus cedere 'to go' simply means a going back.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项：re-「向后」加 cedere「走」，字面就是「往后退」。

senses.title: A withdrawal from a place or claim
senses.titleCN: 从某处或某种主张的退离
senses.definition: the act of withdrawing troops, claims or influence from a position once held
senses.definitionCN: 把军队、主张或影响从曾经占据的位置撤回的行为
senses.example: The recession of the frontier forts followed the treaty.
senses.exampleCN: 条约之后，边境堡垒的驻军向后撤了。
senses.why: Withdrawal extends the physical going back to military and political positions, which are treated as places.
senses.whyCN: 撤离把物理上的后退延伸到军事与政治位置，这些位置被当作「地方」来处理。

senses.title: A hollow or indentation
senses.definition: a hollow place in a surface, a wall or an organ, shaped as if something had been pushed back into it
senses.definitionCN: 表面、墙体或器官上像被压回去而形成的凹处
senses.example: The surgeon worked through a small recession in the bone.
senses.exampleCN: 外科医生从骨头上一个小小的凹陷处入手。
senses.why: A surface that goes back inward forms a recess, so the same noun names the resulting hollow.
senses.whyCN: 向内退的表面形成一个凹处，同一个名词便用来指由此产生的空腔。

senses.title: Gum recession
senses.definition: the drawing back of gum tissue from the crown of a tooth, exposing part of the root
senses.definitionCN: 牙龈组织从牙冠处向后退缩、露出部分牙根的现象
senses.example: Gum recession made the tooth sensitive to cold water.
senses.exampleCN: 牙龈退缩使那颗牙对冷水敏感。
senses.why: Dentistry borrows the image directly: tissue that has drawn back from its usual line is said to have receded.
senses.whyCN: 牙科直接借用这个意象：组织从惯常位置退回去，就说它「退缩」了。

senses.title: The fading of a memory or impression
senses.definition: the gradual fading of a memory, image or feeling as it moves further into the past
senses.definitionCN: 记忆、形象或感觉随时间越退越远而逐渐变淡
senses.example: With each year the recession of that summer grew gentler.
senses.exampleCN: 年复一年，那个夏天的影子退得更温和了。
senses.why: What lies further behind is literally further back, so distance in time is read through the same backward movement.
senses.whyCN: 更早的事在时间上确实更「靠后」，于是时间的距离也通过同一个后退动作来读。

senses.title: A decline in power or importance
senses.definition: a gradual lessening of influence, scale or prominence
senses.definitionCN: 影响力、规模或显著程度的逐渐减弱
senses.example: The recession of the old guilds took a century.
senses.exampleCN: 旧行会的式微经历了一个世纪。
senses.why: Institutions can be said to step back from the centre of things, which lets the noun describe decline without any economic content.
senses.whyCN: 机构可以被说成从中心退开，于是这个名词能描述减退而不带任何经济内容。

senses.title: The outgoing tide
senses.definition: the movement of the sea away from the shore after high water
senses.definitionCN: 高潮之后海水离岸退去的过程
senses.example: Fishermen time their work by the recession of the water.
senses.exampleCN: 渔民按退水的时间安排活计。
senses.why: The sea physically goes back, so the oldest literal sense survives here with no metaphor at all.
senses.whyCN: 海水在物理上确实退回去，因此最古老的字面义在这里毫无比喻地留存下来。

intro.en: Recession comes from Latin recessio 'a going back', built on recedere 'to go back, withdraw', from re- 'back' and cedere 'to go, yield'. The economic sense is twentieth-century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: recession 来自拉丁 recessio「后退」，由 recedere「退回、撤离」构成，即 re-「向后」加 cedere「走、让」。经济义是 20 世纪才有的。年代均为约数。

items.en: Cedere meant 'to go, to yield, to give way' and stands behind cede, proceed, access and a large family of English words.
items.cn: cedere 意为「走、让、退让」，是 cede、proceed、access 以及一大族英语词的来源。

items.en: Re- 'back' plus cedere produced recedere 'to go back, to withdraw, to retire'.
items.cn: re-「向后」加 cedere 构成 recedere「退回、撤离、退去」。

items.en: The noun recessio named the act of going back, and also the hollow left where something has withdrawn.
items.cn: 名词 recessio 既指后退的动作，也指某物退去后留下的凹处。

items.en: French récession carried the noun into English, where it first meant the act of receding in general.
items.cn: 法语 récession 把这个名词带入英语，最初泛指后退的动作。

items.en: From the seventeenth century English recession covered withdrawal, a hollow, and the ebbing of the sea.
items.cn: 自 17 世纪起，英语 recession 涵盖撤离、凹处与海水退落。

items.en: The economic use belongs to the twentieth century, when the business cycle was divided into expansion and recession; the common two-quarter rule is an accounting convention, not part of the word.
items.cn: 经济用法属于 20 世纪，当时商业周期被分为扩张与衰退两段；常见的「连续两季」规则是核算惯例，并非词义的一部分。

note.en: The first group holds the verb and the noun forms built on the same cedere stock, plus one look-alike from a different root; the second holds the names of downturns of different depth.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 cedere 词干的动词与名词形式，另加一个来自不同词根的形近词；第二组是深浅不同的低迷之名。

entries.definition: To move back or fade; the noun recession names the movement or the period in which activity moves back.
entries.definitionCN: 后退或消退；名词 recession 指这个动作，或活动后退的那段时期。

entries.definition: A pause in proceedings or an alcove; it shares the root but names a stopping or a hollow, not a decline.
entries.definitionCN: 议程中的休会或墙上的凹处；同根，但指停顿或空腔，不指下滑。

entries.definition: Describes conditions or forces that produce a recession; it does not name the period itself.
entries.definitionCN: 描述造成衰退的状况或力量；它不指那段时期本身。

entries.definition: From rescindere, built on scindere 'to cut': it means the cancellation of a contract, and is no relative of recession.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 rescindere，词根是 scindere「切」：意为撤销合同，与 recession 并非同族。

entries.definition: Any decline in activity, milder and vaguer than recession; it need not last long enough to be counted.
entries.definitionCN: 活动下滑的通称，比 recession 更轻更模糊；不必持续到足以被计量。

entries.definition: A steep and sudden fall in trade or prices; sharper and less technical than recession.
entries.definitionCN: 贸易或价格的陡然而急剧的下跌；比 recession 更陡，也更不术语化。

entries.definition: A severe downturn lasting years; a recession is the milder phase of the same cycle.
entries.definitionCN: 持续数年的严重低迷；recession 是同一周期中较轻的阶段。

entries.definition: The technical term for output actually shrinking; a recession is a contraction long enough to be officially counted.
entries.definitionCN: 产出实际缩小的技术术语；recession 是持续到被正式计量的收缩。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: a real Latin prefix and root, a real family and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁前缀与词根、真实的同族词与真实的固定说法，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: re- 'back' plus cedere 'to go': a going back, applied to the economy.
normal.cn: re-「向后」加 cedere「走」：往后退，被用到经济上。

normal.en: The family runs recede, recession, recessionary, recess, recessed.
normal.cn: 同族词串成一线：recede、recession、recessionary、recess、recessed。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: economic recession, deep recession, slide into recession, recession fears.
normal.cn: 固定说法：经济衰退、深度衰退、滑入衰退、衰退担忧。

normal.en: The two-quarter rule is a convention of statisticians, not the meaning of the word.
normal.cn: 「连续两季」是统计学家的惯例，不是这个词的含义。

normal.en: Keep cedere 'go' apart from scindere 'cut', which gives rescission.
normal.cn: 把 cedere「走」与 scindere「切」分开，后者给出 rescission。

abstract.en: Picture a tide pulling away from a line of boats left on the mud.
abstract.cn: 想象潮水退离一排搁在泥上的船。

abstract.en: Picture a factory floor where the lights go out one row at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象车间里的灯一排一排地熄灭。

abstract.en: Picture a line on a chart bending back on itself.
abstract.cn: 想象图表上的一条线朝自己弯回去。

examples.en: The recession wiped out a decade of gains in household income.
examples.cn: 这场衰退抹掉了家庭收入十年的增长。

examples.en: Firms that cut training during the recession struggled to hire later.
examples.cn: 衰退期间削减培训的企业，后来招人很吃力。

examples.en: Economists argued over whether the slowdown deserved the name recession.
examples.cn: 经济学家争论这次放缓是否配得上衰退之名。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re（向后）+ cess（走）+ ion」——整体往回走 → 后退、衰退

root: 拉丁 recedere「退回、撤离」= re-「向后」+ cedere「走、让」→ 名词 recessio「后退」→ 英语 recession；经济义为 20 世纪，源自把商业周期分为扩张与衰退。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one backward movement: something goes back, and that going back is read as withdrawal, as a hollow, as receding gums, as fading memory, as declining influence, as an ebbing tide and finally as an economy stepping back.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个后退动作展开：某物往后退，这个后退再依次被读作撤离、凹处、牙龈退缩、记忆变淡、影响力减退、潮水退落，最后是经济倒退一步。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line of boats left on the mud as the water moves back, and a yard where the lights go out row by row.
core.cn: 核心意象：水退之后搁在泥上的一排船，以及灯一排排熄灭的船坞。

branches.en: DECLINE: the economy stepping back and an institution losing its place share one backward image.
branches.cn: 下滑：经济倒退一步与机构失去位置，共享同一个后退意象。

branches.en: GOING BACK: the plain movement and the withdrawal of troops or claims.
branches.cn: 后退：单纯的后退动作，以及军队或主张的撤离。

branches.en: HOLLOW AND GUM: a surface that goes inward, and tissue that draws back from the tooth.
branches.cn: 凹陷与牙龈：向内退的表面，以及从牙齿退开的组织。

branches.en: TIME: what lies further back in time is said to recede from us.
branches.cn: 时间：在时间上更靠后的事，被说成从我们这里退远。

branches.en: TIDE: the sea itself performs the literal movement.
branches.cn: 潮水：大海本身在做这个字面动作。

intro.en: The word is a Latin prefix, a Latin verb root and a noun suffix; the same pieces build a small family of everyday words.
intro.cn: 这个词由一个拉丁前缀、一个拉丁动词词根与一个名词后缀构成；同样的几段还构成一小族日常词。

latinIntro.en: Latin cedere 'to go, yield' gives recede, recess, recession, cede, proceed and access; re- adds the direction back.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 cedere「走、让」衍生出 recede、recess、recession、cede、proceed 与 access；re- 增添「向后」的方向。

items.example: The prefix fixes the direction of the movement.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀确定运动的方向。

items.example: The root runs through a large English family.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根贯穿一大族英语词。

items.example: The compound supplies the verb recede.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合形式提供了动词 recede。

items.example: The Latin noun gave English recession.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词给出英语 recession。

items.example: The suffix turns a verb into a process noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成过程名词。

items.example: The floodwater receded overnight.
items.exampleCN: 洪水一夜之间退去。

items.example: Parliament rose for its summer recess.
items.exampleCN: 议会休会过夏。

items.example: The adjective describes pressure, not the period.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述压力，而非时期。

definition_zh: 经济增长；经济体产出总量的持续增加
definition_en: a sustained increase in the output of goods and services produced by an economy
core_image: 砖窑冒起新烟，外出的人回到镇上进厂，集市摊位一年比一年多
scene: 小镇的砖窑冒起新烟，年轻人从外地回来进厂，集市上的摊位一年比一年多，仓库也不得不加盖一排。 Economists point to rising output and call it economic growth.
sceneCN: 这里 economic growth 指「经济体产出总量的持续增加」（第 1 个义项：一国或一地区所生产的商品与服务总量不断上升）；句意为经济学家把产出上升称为经济增长。图中可辨识物件：冒烟的砖窑、回厂的年轻人、集市摊位、加盖的仓库。

senses.title: A sustained rise in output
senses.definition: a continuing increase in the goods and services an economy produces over time
senses.definitionCN: 一个经济体随时间持续生产出更多商品与服务
senses.example: Economists point to rising output and call it economic growth.
senses.exampleCN: 经济学家把产出上升称为经济增长。
senses.why: The phrase joins a Greek-derived adjective for the management of a household to a native noun for increase, so it names an increase of the whole organized economy.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把源自希腊语、指「家务管理」的形容词，与一个本族表示「增加」的名词组合起来，因此指整个有组织经济的增加。

senses.title: The growth rate
senses.definition: a percentage showing how fast output rises from one period to the next
senses.definitionCN: 表示产出从一个时期到下一个时期上升多快的百分数
senses.example: The economic growth rate averaged four percent that decade.
senses.exampleCN: 那十年间，经济增长率平均为百分之四。
senses.why: A process noun readily stands for its own measure, which is why the phrase can be followed by rate.
senses.whyCN: 过程名词容易转指自身的度量，因此这个短语后面可以直接接 rate。

senses.title: Growth per head
senses.definition: growth measured after dividing total output by the number of people, so that population change is taken into account
senses.definitionCN: 把总产出按人口分摊后再衡量的增长，从而把人口变动计入
senses.example: Per-head economic growth lagged behind the national total.
senses.exampleCN: 人均经济增长落后于全国总量。
senses.why: Because a larger population can raise the total while leaving each person no better off, the phrase is often qualified by per head.
senses.whyCN: 因为人口增加可以抬高总量而个人并未变好，这个短语常被加上「人均」的限定。

senses.title: Extensive growth
senses.definition: growth achieved by adding more land, labour and capital rather than by using them better
senses.definitionCN: 靠增加土地、劳动与资本投入而非提高使用效率来实现的增长
senses.example: Extensive economic growth ran out of new land to plough.
senses.exampleCN: 粗放型经济增长把可开垦的新地都用尽了。
senses.why: When the increase comes from more inputs, economists call it extensive, and the phrase takes the adjective as a label.
senses.whyCN: 当增加来自更多投入时，经济学家称之为粗放型，这个短语便带上该形容词作为标签。

senses.title: Intensive growth
senses.definition: growth achieved by raising productivity, so that the same inputs yield more output
senses.definitionCN: 靠提高生产率、使同样投入产出更多而实现的增长
senses.example: Intensive economic growth followed the rebuilding of the mills.
senses.exampleCN: 磨坊重建之后，出现了集约型经济增长。
senses.why: The mirror label marks growth from better methods rather than from more hands, and the phrase carries both.
senses.whyCN: 这个镜像标签标记来自更好方法而非更多人工的增长，这个短语两者都能承载。

senses.title: The boom that growth brings
senses.definition: the period of fuller shops, more jobs and rising confidence that accompanies rising output
senses.definitionCN: 伴随产出上升而来的店铺更热闹、岗位更多、信心更高的时期
senses.example: Three years of economic growth filled the high street again.
senses.exampleCN: 三年的经济增长让商业街重新热闹起来。
senses.why: By metonymy the cause stands for its effects, so the phrase can name the prosperous stretch rather than the statistic.
senses.whyCN: 通过转喻，原因代替了结果，因此这个短语可以指那段繁荣时期，而不只是那个统计量。

senses.title: Sustainable growth
senses.definition: growth that does not exhaust the resources or damage the systems on which future output depends
senses.definitionCN: 不会耗尽资源、也不破坏未来产出所依赖的系统的增长
senses.example: Sustainable economic growth requires cleaner power.
senses.exampleCN: 可持续的经济增长需要更清洁的电力。
senses.why: Once the environmental cost is counted, the phrase takes a qualifier that asks whether the increase can continue.
senses.whyCN: 一旦把环境成本计入，这个短语就带上一个限定语，追问这种增加能否持续。

senses.title: Growth as a policy target
senses.definition: the pursuit of rising output as the chief aim of government policy
senses.definitionCN: 把产出上升当作政府政策的首要目标来追求
senses.example: The budget put economic growth ahead of every other aim.
senses.exampleCN: 预算把经济增长排在所有其他目标之前。
senses.why: A measured increase can become an objective, and the phrase then names a goal rather than a fact.
senses.whyCN: 一个被度量的增加可以变成目标，这个短语于是指一项追求而非一个事实。

intro.en: Economic growth joins economic, from Greek oikonomia 'household management' through Latin oeconomia and French économique, with growth, a native English noun from the verb grow. The phrase belongs to modern economics. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: economic growth 由 economic 与 growth 组合而成；economic 出自希腊 oikonomia「家务管理」，经拉丁 oeconomia 与法语 économique 进入英语；growth 则是英语本族名词，源自动词 grow。这个短语属于现代经济学。年代均为约数。

items.en: Oikos meant 'house, household', the unit whose resources were to be managed.
items.cn: oikos 意为「房屋、家户」，即其资源需要被管理的单位。

items.en: Oikos plus nomos 'managing, rule, custom' gave oikonomia, the art of running a household; nomos itself comes from nemein 'to manage, distribute'.
items.cn: oikos 加 nomos「管理、规则、习俗」构成 oikonomia，即治家之术；nomos 本身来自 nemein「管理、分配」。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek word as oeconomia, still meaning household management rather than a national economy.
items.cn: 拉丁把希腊词借作 oeconomia，仍指家务管理，而不是国家经济。

items.en: French économique supplied English economic in the seventeenth century; the sense 'of a national economy' developed later, in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 法语 économique 在 17 世纪提供英语 economic；「属于国家经济」的义项则较晚，在 19 世纪发展出来。

items.en: Grow is native: Old English growan 'to grow, increase' is a strong verb whose past tense was grew and whose participle was grown.
items.cn: grow 是英语本族词：古英语 growan「生长、增加」是强变化动词，过去式为 grew，过去分词为 grown。

items.en: The phrase took its present meaning with national accounting and development economics in the twentieth century, when output could be measured year by year.
items.cn: 这个短语在 20 世纪随国民核算与发展经济学取得今义，当时产出已能逐年计量。

note.en: The first group holds phrases that are often substituted for this one but measure or mean something else; the second holds plain words for things getting larger.
note.cn: 第一组是常被拿来替换本短语、但所测或所指并不相同的说法；第二组是「变大」的朴素说法。

entries.definition: A wider idea that includes institutions, health, education and distribution, not only rising output.
entries.definitionCN: 更宽的概念，包含制度、健康、教育与分配，而不只是产出上升。

entries.definition: The upswing of the business cycle; it may be shorter and more temporary than growth.
entries.definitionCN: 商业周期的上行段；可能比 growth 更短、更暂时。

entries.definition: The amount produced at a moment; growth is the change in that amount over time.
entries.definitionCN: 某一时点生产出的数量；growth 是这一数量随时间的变化。

entries.definition: The percentage by which output rises; it reports growth rather than naming the process.
entries.definitionCN: 产出上升的百分数；它报告增长，而不命名这个过程。

entries.definition: A literal description of the same fact, with no economic framing.
entries.definitionCN: 对同一事实的字面描述，不带经济学框架。

entries.definition: A rapid, often speculative upturn; it suggests intensity and eventual bust rather than steady gain.
entries.definitionCN: 迅速且常带投机的上行；暗示猛烈以及随后的回落，而非稳步增益。

entries.definition: A condition of comfort and success; it is a state people enjoy, not a measured increase.
entries.definitionCN: 富足顺遂的状态；是人们享受的境况，而非被度量的增加。

entries.definition: Growth as measured by gross domestic product; it is one yardstick of economic growth, not the whole idea.
entries.definitionCN: 以国内生产总值衡量的增长；是经济增长的一种尺子，而非全部。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: a real Greek root, a native English verb and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的希腊词根、英语本族动词与真实的固定说法，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: oikos 'house' plus nomos 'management': the household whose output is now counted by the nation.
normal.cn: oikos「家」加 nomos「管理」：这个家户的产出如今由国家来计数。

normal.en: grow is native Old English; growth adds the noun suffix -th to the verb.
normal.cn: grow 是古英语本族词；growth 是在动词后加名词后缀 -th。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: sustained economic growth, rapid economic growth, economic growth rate.
normal.cn: 固定说法：持续经济增长、快速增长、经济增长率。

normal.en: The pair is common in policy: promote growth, slow growth, inclusive growth.
normal.cn: 这对搭配常见于政策话语：促进增长、增长放缓、包容性增长。

normal.en: Keep growth apart from development: one is output, the other includes institutions and well-being.
normal.cn: 把 growth 与 development 分开：前者是产出，后者还包含制度与福祉。

abstract.en: Picture a brick kiln smoking again after years of silence.
abstract.cn: 想象一座沉寂多年的砖窑重新冒烟。

abstract.en: Picture a market that needs one more row of stalls each season.
abstract.cn: 想象集市每季都得多添一排摊位。

abstract.en: Picture a line on a chart climbing while a whole town changes underneath it.
abstract.cn: 想象图表上一条线往上走，整座小镇在它下面改变。

examples.en: Sustained economic growth lifted millions out of rural poverty.
examples.cn: 持续的经济增长使数百万人摆脱农村贫困。

examples.en: The report asks whether economic growth can continue without new energy sources.
examples.cn: 报告追问：没有新能源，经济增长能否持续。

examples.en: Per-head economic growth stalled even as the total rose.
examples.cn: 总量上升之际，人均经济增长却停滞了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「economic（经济的）+ growth（增长）」——经济这块蛋糕一年比一年大 → 经济增长

root: economic 出自希腊 oikonomia「家务管理」= oikos「家」+ nomos「管理」→ 拉丁 oeconomia → 法语 économique → 英语 economic；growth 为古英语 growan「生长」加名词后缀 -th。短语义属 20 世纪国民核算。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one increase: total output rises, and then that rise is read as a rate, as a share per head, as more inputs, as better methods, as a boom, as a limit and finally as a policy aim.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个增加展开：总产出上升，这个上升再依次被读作一个比率、一份人均份额、更多投入、更好方法、一段繁荣、一条限度，最后是一项政策目标。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a kiln smoking again, workers returning, and one more row of market stalls each season.
core.cn: 核心意象：砖窑重新冒烟，工人回厂，集市每季多出一排摊位。

branches.en: OUTPUT AND RATE: the increase itself, and the percentage that reports it.
branches.cn: 产出与比率：增加本身，以及报告它的百分数。

branches.en: SHARE AND BOOM: growth divided among people, and the fuller shops it brings.
branches.cn: 份额与繁荣：增长分到每个人头上，以及它带来的更热闹的店铺。

branches.en: INPUTS AND METHODS: the same increase can come from more hands or from better hands.
branches.cn: 投入与方法：同一种增加可以来自更多人手，也可以来自更巧的手。

branches.en: LIMIT: the question whether the increase can keep going without exhausting its base.
branches.cn: 限度：这种增加能否在不耗尽根基的情况下继续。

branches.en: AIM: a measured increase becomes something a government tries to produce.
branches.cn: 目标：一个被度量的增加，变成政府努力去促成的对象。

intro.en: The phrase can be read in five pieces: two Greek roots, a Latin borrowing, an adjective suffix, and a native English verb with its noun suffix.
intro.cn: 这个短语可拆成五段：两个希腊词根、一个拉丁借词、一个形容词后缀，以及一个英语本族动词连同它的名词后缀。

latinIntro.en: Greek oikos and nomos reached English through Latin oeconomia and French économique; grow is native Old English and has no Latin ancestor.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 oikos 与 nomos 经拉丁 oeconomia 与法语 économique 进入英语；grow 是古英语本族词，没有拉丁来源。

items.example: The root supplies the household image behind economy.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供 economy 背后的「家户」意象。

items.example: The root names the ordering of the household.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指家户的秩序安排。

items.example: The compound is the direct ancestor of economy.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词是 economy 的直系祖先。

items.example: Latin kept the household sense for centuries.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语把「家户」义保留了许多世纪。

items.example: The modern sense is tied to national economies.
items.exampleCN: 现代义与国民经济相连。

items.example: The suffix builds the adjective from the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀由名词构成形容词。

items.example: The native verb carries no Latin root.
items.exampleCN: 这个本族动词不带拉丁词根。

items.example: The suffix turns grow into the noun growth.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把 grow 变成名词 growth。

items.example: Growth is the noun of the native verb.
items.exampleCN: growth 是本族动词的名词形式。

latinEntries.structure: oeconomia, oeconomiae (n., first declension, from Greek)

definition_zh: 经济扩张；产出与就业上升的阶段
definition_en: a period in which an economy's output, employment and spending are growing
core_image: 港口的吊机昼夜不停，新厂房沿公路一排排立起，招工的人守在车站出口
scene: 港口的吊机昼夜不停，新厂房沿公路一排排立起来，招工的人守在车站出口，连旧仓库也被租空。 Shipping records show a year of economic expansion along the coast.
sceneCN: 这里 economic expansion 指「产出、就业与支出都在增长的阶段」（第 1 个义项：经济体规模整体扩大的时期）；句意为航运记录显示沿海经历了一年的经济扩张。图中可辨识物件：昼夜运转的吊机、新建厂房、车站招工牌、租空的旧仓库。

pos.zh: 经济扩张；经济上行阶段

derivatives.zh: 扩张主义的 / 扩张主义者

senses.title: A period of growing output
senses.definition: a stretch of time in which an economy produces, employs and spends more than before
senses.definitionCN: 一个经济体比此前生产更多、雇用更多、支出更多的时期
senses.example: Shipping records show a year of economic expansion along the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 航运记录显示沿海经历了一年的经济扩张。
senses.why: Expansion is the noun of a Latin verb meaning 'to spread out', so the phrase pictures the economy opening outward in every direction at once.
senses.whyCN: expansion 是一个意为「展开」的拉丁动词的名词，因此这个短语把经济想象成同时向四面八方铺开。

senses.title: The upswing of the cycle
senses.definition: the rising phase of the business cycle, between one trough and the next peak
senses.definitionCN: 商业周期中上升的那一段，位于一个谷底与下一个峰顶之间
senses.example: The last economic expansion lasted almost a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 上一轮经济扩张持续了近十年。
senses.why: Once cycles are drawn as waves, the rising half needs a name, and expansion is the natural opposite of contraction.
senses.whyCN: 一旦把周期画成波浪，上升的一半就需要名字，而 expansion 正是 contraction 的自然对立面。

senses.title: A firm widening its scale
senses.definition: the growth of a company through new plants, markets or staff
senses.definitionCN: 企业通过新工厂、新市场或新员工实现的增长
senses.example: The mill's economic expansion added two shifts and a rail siding.
senses.exampleCN: 这家磨坊的规模扩张增加了两个班次和一条铁路侧线。
senses.why: The same verb describes anything spreading wider, so a single business can expand exactly as an economy does.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动词可描述任何变宽的事物，因此单个企业的扩张与整个经济的扩张用的是同一个词。

senses.title: Territorial expansion
senses.definition: the extension of a state's territory or a people's settled area
senses.definitionCN: 国家领土或族群定居区域的向外延伸
senses.example: Railways drove the economic expansion of the frontier.
senses.exampleCN: 铁路推动了边疆地区的版图扩张。
senses.why: Physical spreading is the oldest sense of the root, and land is the most literal thing an economy can spread across.
senses.whyCN: 物理上的铺展是这个词根最古老的义项，而土地正是经济最字面地可以铺展开的对象。

senses.title: Expansion of demand
senses.definition: a rise in total spending by households, firms and government
senses.definitionCN: 家庭、企业与政府总支出上升
senses.example: Demand-led economic expansion pushed up imports.
senses.exampleCN: 需求带动的经济扩张推高了进口。
senses.why: Economists split the economy into sides, so expansion can be located on the demand side as well as in total output.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家把经济分成几侧，因此扩张既可以说在总产出上，也可以说在需求一侧。

senses.title: Expansion of credit
senses.definition: a growth in lending and borrowing that lets spending outrun current income
senses.definitionCN: 借贷规模增长，使支出得以超过当期收入
senses.example: Cheap credit financed the economic expansion of those years.
senses.exampleCN: 廉价信贷为那些年的经济扩张提供了资金。
senses.why: Credit is one of the channels through which an economy widens, and the phrase takes the channel as its qualifier.
senses.whyCN: 信贷是经济变宽的渠道之一，这个短语便把渠道拿来作限定语。

senses.title: Expansion of capacity
senses.definition: the building of more plant, equipment and infrastructure so that more can be produced later
senses.definitionCN: 兴建更多厂房、设备与基础设施，以便日后生产更多
senses.example: Capacity-led economic expansion takes years to show in output.
senses.exampleCN: 产能带动的经济扩张要多年才体现在产出上。
senses.why: Because widening the ability to produce precedes the increase itself, the phrase can point at investment rather than at results.
senses.whyCN: 由于生产能力的扩大先于增加本身，这个短语可以指向投资而非结果。

senses.title: Expansion of the money supply
senses.definition: an increase in the quantity of money circulating in an economy
senses.definitionCN: 经济体中流通的货币数量增加
senses.example: Monetary economic expansion showed up first in asset prices.
senses.exampleCN: 货币层面的经济扩张最先体现在资产价格上。
senses.why: The central bank can widen the money stock directly, and the phrase borrows the same image for that measure.
senses.whyCN: 央行可以直接把货币存量放宽，这个短语便为那项度量借用了同一个意象。

intro.en: Economic expansion joins economic, from Greek oikonomia through Latin oeconomia, with expansion, from Latin expansio, built on expandere 'to spread out', from ex- 'out' and pandere 'to spread'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: economic expansion 由 economic（出自希腊 oikonomia，经拉丁 oeconomia）与 expansion 组合而成；expansion 来自拉丁 expansio，由 expandere「展开」构成，即 ex-「向外」加 pandere「铺展」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Pandere meant 'to spread out, to unfold', and stands behind expand, expanse and expansion.
items.cn: pandere 意为「铺展开、展开」，是 expand、expanse 与 expansion 的来源。

items.en: Ex- 'out' plus pandere gave expandere 'to spread out, to open wide'.
items.cn: ex-「向外」加 pandere 构成 expandere「铺展开、张开」。

items.en: The noun expansio named the act of spreading out and the space so opened.
items.cn: 名词 expansio 指铺展的动作，也指由此张开的空间。

items.en: English expansion is recorded from the seventeenth century, first for physical spreading and then for wider extension of any kind.
items.cn: 英语 expansion 自 17 世纪有记录，先指物理上的铺展，后指任何意义上的向外延伸。

items.en: The economic sense developed with the language of business cycles in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries.
items.cn: 经济义随 19 至 20 世纪的商业周期话语发展出来。

items.en: Expansion is not related to expend or expenditure, which come from expendere, built on pendere 'to weigh'; the two roots only sound alike.
items.cn: expansion 与 expend、expenditure 并无亲缘，后者来自 expendere，词根是 pendere「称重」；两个词根只是听起来相近。

note.en: The first group holds terms often swapped for this phrase, including one that merely looks related; the second holds words for things getting wider or busier.
note.cn: 第一组是常与本短语互换的说法，其中含一个只是看起来相关的词；第二组是「变宽、变热闹」的词。

entries.definition: The sustained rise in output over years; expansion is one phase within that trend, and can be shorter.
entries.definitionCN: 多年间产出的持续上升；expansion 是这一趋势中的一个阶段，可能更短。

entries.definition: Widening of any kind; the phrase economic expansion narrows it to the economy.
entries.definitionCN: 任何意义上的变宽；短语 economic expansion 把它收窄到经济。

entries.definition: From expendere, built on pendere 'to weigh': money spent, not space opened, and no relative of expansion.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 expendere，词根是 pendere「称重」：指花出去的钱，而非张开的空间，与 expansion 并非同族。

entries.definition: Means wide in extent or open in manner; it can describe a mood as easily as a territory.
entries.definitionCN: 指范围广阔或态度开朗；既能形容领土，也能形容心情。

entries.definition: The upward movement of a cycle; it is nearly the same as expansion in cycle talk.
entries.definitionCN: 周期的向上运动；在周期话语中与 expansion 几乎相同。

entries.definition: A rapid upturn, often with speculation; it implies more heat and a sharper end than expansion.
entries.definitionCN: 迅速的上行，常带投机；比 expansion 更热，也更暗示陡然的结束。

entries.definition: A climb back toward an earlier level; expansion need not be recovering anything lost.
entries.definitionCN: 朝此前水平回升；expansion 并不一定是在收回失去的东西。

entries.definition: A literal word for something becoming broader, with no economic measurement attached.
entries.definitionCN: 字面表示某物变宽的词，不带经济度量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: a real Latin prefix and root, a real family and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁前缀与词根、真实的同族词与真实的固定说法，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ex- 'out' plus pandere 'spread': the economy spreads outward.
normal.cn: ex-「向外」加 pandere「铺展」：经济向外铺开。

normal.en: The family runs expand, expansion, expansive, expansionary, expansionist.
normal.cn: 同族词串成一线：expand、expansion、expansive、expansionary、expansionist。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: rapid economic expansion, export-led expansion, expansionary policy.
normal.cn: 固定说法：快速经济扩张、出口带动的扩张、扩张性政策。

normal.en: Expansion is the mirror of contraction in cycle talk.
normal.cn: 在周期话语中，expansion 是 contraction 的镜像。

normal.en: Do not link it to expenditure: that root is pendere 'to weigh'.
normal.cn: 别把它和 expenditure 联系起来：那个词根是 pendere「称重」。

abstract.en: Picture cranes that never sleep and a road lined with new roofs.
abstract.cn: 想象吊机昼夜不停，公路两旁全是新屋顶。

abstract.en: Picture a map whose settled edge keeps moving outward.
abstract.cn: 想象地图上有人定居的边缘不断向外移动。

abstract.en: Picture a balloon widening in every direction at once, not just upward.
abstract.cn: 想象气球同时向四面八方变宽，而不只是向上。

examples.en: Export-led economic expansion brought foreign earnings into the valley.
examples.cn: 出口带动的经济扩张把外汇收入带进谷地。

examples.en: The bank warned that credit-driven economic expansion rarely ends quietly.
examples.cn: 银行警告说，信贷驱动的经济扩张很少平静收场。

examples.en: Capacity-led economic expansion may take years to appear in the figures.
examples.cn: 产能带动的经济扩张可能要多年才体现在数字上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「economic（经济的）+ expansion（向外铺开）」——整块经济往外摊开 → 经济扩张

root: economic 出自希腊 oikonomia「家务管理」（oikos 家 + nomos 管理），经拉丁 oeconomia 与法语；expansion 出自拉丁 expandere「展开」= ex-「向外」+ pandere「铺展」→ expansio；与 expendere（pendere 称重）无亲缘。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one widening: the economy spreads outward, and that spreading is read as a cycle phase, as a firm's growth, as new territory, as more demand, as more credit, as more capacity and finally as more money.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个「变宽」展开：经济向外铺开，这个铺开再依次被读作周期阶段、企业成长、新领土、更多需求、更多信贷、更多产能，最后是更多货币。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: cranes that never stop, a road lined with new roofs, and an old warehouse rented out.
core.cn: 核心意象：不停歇的吊机、两旁全是新屋顶的公路，以及被租空的旧仓库。

branches.en: OUTPUT AND CYCLE: the widening of the whole economy, and its place as the rising half of a wave.
branches.cn: 产出与周期：整个经济的变宽，以及它作为波浪上升的一半所处的位置。

branches.en: FIRM AND LAND: one business spreads wider, and a people pushes its settled edge outward.
branches.cn: 企业与土地：单个企业变宽，一个族群把定居边缘向外推。

branches.en: DEMAND AND CREDIT: spending and lending are two channels through which the widening runs.
branches.cn: 需求与信贷：支出与借贷是这种变宽流经的两条渠道。

branches.en: CAPACITY: the ability to produce is widened before the output arrives.
branches.cn: 产能：生产能力先在扩大，产出随后才到。

branches.en: MONEY: the central bank widens the stock of money itself.
branches.cn: 货币：央行直接把货币存量放宽。

intro.en: The phrase combines a Greek-derived adjective and a Latin noun; the noun can be read as a prefix, a verb root and a process suffix.
intro.cn: 这个短语由一个希腊来源的形容词与一个拉丁名词组合而成；名词部分可拆成前缀、动词词根与过程后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin pandere 'to spread' gives expand, expanse, expansion and expansive; ex- adds the direction outward.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 pandere「铺展」衍生出 expand、expanse、expansion 与 expansive；ex- 增添「向外」的方向。

items.example: The prefix sends the spreading outward.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把铺展送向外面。

items.example: The root supplies the image of opening wide.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「张开」的意象。

items.example: The compound supplied the English verb expand.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合形式提供了英语动词 expand。

items.example: The Latin noun gave English expansion.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词给出英语 expansion。

items.example: The suffix turns the verb into a process noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成过程名词。

items.example: The firm expanded into two new markets.
items.exampleCN: 这家公司扩张进入两个新市场。

items.example: The adjective marks policy that deliberately expands.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词标记有意扩张的政策。

items.example: The adjective describes extent or temperament.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述范围或性情。

definition_zh: 经济收缩；产出与就业下降的阶段
definition_en: a period in which an economy's output, employment and spending are shrinking
core_image: 集装箱堆到三层高却没人来提，班次一减再减，装卸工在休息棚里等消息
scene: 码头的集装箱堆到三层高却没人来提，班次一减再减，装卸工在休息棚里等消息，连食堂也缩短了开饭时间。 Freight volumes fell for three quarters, a clear sign of economic contraction.
sceneCN: 这里 economic contraction 指「产出、就业与支出都在下降的阶段」（第 1 个义项：经济体规模整体缩小的时期）；句意为货运量连续三个季度下滑，是经济收缩的明显迹象。图中可辨识物件：堆高的集装箱、减少的班次表、休息棚、缩短营业的食堂。

pos.zh: 经济收缩；经济下行阶段

senses.title: A period of shrinking output
senses.definition: a stretch of time in which an economy produces, employs and spends less than before
senses.definitionCN: 一个经济体比此前生产更少、雇用更少、支出更少的时期
senses.example: Freight volumes fell for three quarters, a clear sign of economic contraction.
senses.exampleCN: 货运量连续三个季度下滑，是经济收缩的明显迹象。
senses.why: Contraction is the noun of a Latin verb meaning 'to draw together', so the phrase pictures the economy pulled in on itself.
senses.whyCN: contraction 是一个意为「拉到一起」的拉丁动词的名词，因此这个短语把经济想象成向内收拢。

senses.title: The downswing of the cycle
senses.definition: the falling phase of the business cycle, between one peak and the next trough
senses.definitionCN: 商业周期中下降的那一段，位于一个峰顶与下一个谷底之间
senses.example: The last economic contraction was short but steep.
senses.exampleCN: 上一轮经济收缩虽短，却很陡。
senses.why: Drawn as a wave, the falling half needs a name, and contraction is the natural opposite of expansion.
senses.whyCN: 把周期画成波浪，下降的一半就需要名字，而 contraction 正是 expansion 的自然对立面。

senses.title: A firm cutting its scale
senses.definition: the shrinking of a company through closed plants, fewer staff or narrower markets
senses.definitionCN: 企业通过关厂、减员或收缩市场而缩小
senses.example: The chain's economic contraction closed forty stores.
senses.exampleCN: 这家连锁店的规模收缩关掉了四十家门店。
senses.why: The verb applies to anything being drawn smaller, so one business can contract exactly as an economy does.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词可用于任何被拉小的事物，因此单个企业的收缩与整个经济的收缩用的是同一个词。

senses.title: Muscle contraction
senses.definition: the shortening and thickening of a muscle when it does work
senses.definitionCN: 肌肉发力时变短变粗的过程
senses.example: Each contraction of the heart pushes blood onward.
senses.exampleCN: 心脏每一次收缩都把血向前推送。
senses.why: Physiology took the literal drawing-together of fibres, which is the clearest physical instance of the root.
senses.whyCN: 生理学取用了纤维字面上的「拉到一起」，这是这个词根最清楚的物理实例。

senses.title: Shrinking in volume
senses.definition: the decrease in size of a material or object when it cools, dries or is compressed
senses.definitionCN: 材料或物体在冷却、干燥或被压缩时尺寸变小
senses.example: The contraction of the clay opened cracks along the rim.
senses.exampleCN: 陶土收缩，沿口沿裂开。
senses.why: When a body draws in, its volume falls, and the noun names that measurable change.
senses.whyCN: 物体向内收，体积就减小，这个名词指称那种可度量的变化。

senses.title: Contraction of credit
senses.definition: a fall in lending as banks tighten terms or lose confidence
senses.definitionCN: 银行收紧条件或失去信心而导致贷款减少
senses.example: Credit contraction hit small builders first.
senses.exampleCN: 信贷收缩首先打击了小型建筑商。
senses.why: Lending is one channel through which an economy draws in, and the phrase names the channel rather than the total.
senses.whyCN: 放贷是经济向内收的一条渠道，这个短语指渠道而非总量。

senses.title: Contraction of spending
senses.definition: a cut in household, business or government spending
senses.definitionCN: 家庭、企业或政府支出的削减
senses.example: Household spending contraction deepened the factory slowdown.
senses.exampleCN: 家庭支出收缩加深了工厂的放缓。
senses.why: Spending is the demand side of the same shrinking, and the phrase can point there instead of at output.
senses.whyCN: 支出是同一个缩小的需求一侧，这个短语可以指向那里而非产出。

senses.title: Contraction of the money supply
senses.definition: a decrease in the quantity of money circulating in an economy
senses.definitionCN: 经济体中流通的货币数量减少
senses.example: Monetary contraction followed the panic of that autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 货币层面的收缩紧随那年秋天的恐慌而来。
senses.why: The central bank can draw the money stock in directly, and the phrase borrows the same image for that measure.
senses.whyCN: 央行可以直接把货币存量收紧，这个短语便为那项度量借用同一个意象。

intro.en: Economic contraction joins economic, from Greek oikonomia through Latin oeconomia, with contraction, from Latin contractio, built on contrahere 'to draw together', from con- 'together' and trahere 'to draw'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: economic contraction 由 economic（出自希腊 oikonomia，经拉丁 oeconomia）与 contraction 组合而成；contraction 来自拉丁 contractio，由 contrahere「拉到一起」构成，即 con-「共同」加 trahere「拉」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Trahere meant 'to draw, to pull' and stands behind tractor, attract, extract and a large English family.
items.cn: trahere 意为「拉、拖」，是 tractor、attract、extract 以及一大族英语词的来源。

items.en: Con- 'together' plus trahere gave contrahere 'to draw together, to tighten'; it also came to mean to conclude an agreement.
items.cn: con-「共同」加 trahere 构成 contrahere「拉到一起、收紧」；它后来也指缔结协议。

items.en: The noun contractio named the drawing together of anything, from limbs to legal terms.
items.cn: 名词 contractio 指把任何东西拉到一起，从肢体到法律条款都包括。

items.en: English contraction is recorded from the sixteenth century for the shortening of words and for the action of muscles.
items.cn: 英语 contraction 自 16 世纪有记录，指词的缩短以及肌肉的动作。

items.en: The same Latin verb produced contract as a noun for an agreement, since terms are drawn together into one binding arrangement; that sense diverged from the physical one.
items.cn: 同一个拉丁动词还产生名词 contract「合同」，因为条款被拉到一起成为一份有约束力的安排；那一义与物理义分道而行。

items.en: The economic sense developed with business-cycle language in the twentieth century, when contraction became the measurable opposite of expansion.
items.cn: 经济义随 20 世纪的商业周期话语发展出来，此时 contraction 成为 expansion 可度量的对立面。

note.en: The first group holds terms often swapped for this phrase, including two from the same root that mean something else; the second holds words for things getting smaller.
note.cn: 第一组是常与本短语互换的说法，其中含两个同根却另有所指的词；第二组是「变小」的词。

entries.definition: A contraction long enough to be officially counted; contraction can be shorter and is the measurable movement itself.
entries.definitionCN: 持续到被正式计量的收缩；contraction 可以更短，且就是那个可度量的运动本身。

entries.definition: Shrinking of any kind, including muscles and word forms; the phrase narrows it to the economy.
entries.definitionCN: 任何意义上的缩小，包括肌肉与词形；短语把它收窄到经济。

entries.definition: From the same verb 'to draw together', but as a noun it means a binding agreement, not a shrinking.
entries.definitionCN: 同出「拉到一起」这个动词，但作名词时指有约束力的协议，而非缩小。

entries.definition: From constringere, built on stringere 'to bind tight': a narrowing by pressure, not a settling inward.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 constringere，词根是 stringere「束紧」：指受压变窄，而非向内收拢。

entries.definition: Any decline in activity; vaguer and milder than a measured contraction.
entries.definitionCN: 活动下滑的通称；比可度量的 contraction 更模糊、更轻。

entries.definition: A literal getting smaller, often of material or stock; it lacks the cyclical meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 字面上的变小，多指材料或存货；不带周期含义。

entries.definition: A general falling off in amount or quality; it makes no claim about measurement.
entries.definitionCN: 数量或质量的普遍下降；不涉及度量。

entries.definition: A deliberate policy of cutting spending; it may cause contraction but is a choice, not the movement.
entries.definitionCN: 有意的削减开支政策；它可能造成收缩，但那是选择而非运动本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: a real Latin prefix and root, a real family and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁前缀与词根、真实的同族词与真实的固定说法，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: con- 'together' plus trahere 'draw': the economy draws in on itself.
normal.cn: con-「共同」加 trahere「拉」：经济把自己往里收。

normal.en: The family runs contract, contraction, contractionary, contractile, contractor.
normal.cn: 同族词串成一线：contract、contraction、contractionary、contractile、contractor。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: sharp economic contraction, contractionary policy, global contraction.
normal.cn: 固定说法：急剧经济收缩、紧缩性政策、全球收缩。

normal.en: In cycle talk contraction is the mirror of expansion.
normal.cn: 在周期话语中，contraction 是 expansion 的镜像。

normal.en: Keep it apart from constriction, whose root is stringere 'to bind'.
normal.cn: 把它与 constriction 分开，后者词根是 stringere「束紧」。

abstract.en: Picture stacked containers that nobody comes to collect.
abstract.cn: 想象堆高的集装箱，没人来提。

abstract.en: Picture a shift board with more and more lines crossed out.
abstract.cn: 想象班次表上被划掉的线越来越多。

abstract.en: Picture a hand slowly closing around a coin.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手慢慢把一枚硬币握紧。

examples.en: A sharp economic contraction usually hits young workers first.
examples.cn: 急剧的经济收缩通常最先冲击年轻工人。

examples.en: The central bank cut rates to pull the economy out of contraction.
examples.cn: 央行降息，力图把经济拉出收缩。

examples.en: Credit contraction turned a small shock into a long slump.
examples.cn: 信贷收缩把一次小冲击拖成了长期低迷。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「economic（经济的）+ contraction（往里收）」——整块经济往内收 → 经济收缩

root: economic 出自希腊 oikonomia「家务管理」（oikos 家 + nomos 管理），经拉丁 oeconomia 与法语；contraction 出自拉丁 contrahere「拉到一起」= con-「共同」+ trahere「拉」→ contractio；同根名词 contract 指合同，义已分化。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one drawing-in: the economy pulls inward, and that pulling is read as a cycle phase, as a firm's shrink, as a muscle shortening, as a volume loss, as less credit, as less spending and finally as less money.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个「向内收」展开：经济往里收，这个收拢再依次被读作周期阶段、企业缩小、肌肉变短、体积减小、更少信贷、更少支出，最后是更少货币。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: stacked containers nobody collects, a shift board crossed out, and a hand closing around a coin.
core.cn: 核心意象：无人来提的堆高集装箱、被划掉的班次表，以及慢慢握紧硬币的手。

branches.en: OUTPUT AND CYCLE: the whole economy pulls in, and that pull is the falling half of a wave.
branches.cn: 产出与周期：整个经济向内收，这个收拢就是波浪下降的一半。

branches.en: FIRM AND SPENDING: one business shrinks, and households cut what they buy.
branches.cn: 企业与支出：单个企业缩小，家庭削减购买。

branches.en: BODY AND MATTER: a muscle shortens, and a material loses volume.
branches.cn: 身体与物质：肌肉变短，材料失去体积。

branches.en: CREDIT: lending is the channel through which the pull runs fastest.
branches.cn: 信贷：放贷是这种收拢传导最快的渠道。

branches.en: MONEY: the central bank draws the stock of money in by design.
branches.cn: 货币：央行有意把货币存量收紧。

intro.en: The phrase combines a Greek-derived adjective and a Latin noun; the noun can be read as a prefix, a verb root and a process suffix.
