latinIntro.en: Latin trahere 'to draw' gives contract, contraction, tractor, attract and extract; con- adds the idea of drawing together.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 trahere「拉」衍生出 contract、contraction、tractor、attract 与 extract；con- 增添「拉到一起」的意思。

items.example: The prefix makes the drawing collective.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀使「拉」成为向内的合拢。

items.example: The root runs through tractor and attract.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根贯穿 tractor 与 attract。

items.example: The compound also named the making of an agreement.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合形式还指缔结协议。

items.example: The Latin noun gave English contraction.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词给出英语 contraction。

items.example: The suffix turns the verb into a process noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成过程名词。

items.structure: contract (English verb and noun from Latin contractus)
items.example: The two senses split long ago.
items.exampleCN: 这两个义项早已分化。

items.example: The adjective marks policy that deliberately tightens.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词标记有意收紧的政策。

items.example: Muscle fibre is contractile tissue.
items.exampleCN: 肌纤维是可收缩的组织。

definition_zh: 国内生产总值；一国境内一定时期内生产的最终产品与服务总值
definition_en: the total market value of all final goods and services produced within a country in a given period
core_image: 会议桌上摊开一年的账本，几个人把全国做成的每一件事折算成一个总数
scene: 统计局的会议室里，几个人把一年的产出逐项加总，想用一张表说明整个国家到底做出了多少东西。 The report compares gross domestic product across two decades.
sceneCN: 这里 gross domestic product 指「一国境内一定时期内生产的最终产品与服务总值」（第 1 个义项：按市场价格衡量的境内最终产出总量）；句意为这份报告比较了二十年的国内生产总值。图中可辨识物件：摊开的账本、加总表、计算器、墙上地图。

collocations.zh: 国内生产总值平减指数

senses.title: The total value of domestic output
senses.definition: the market value of all final goods and services produced inside a country's borders in a period
senses.definitionCN: 在一定时期内、于一国国境之内生产的所有最终商品与服务的市场价值
senses.example: The report compares gross domestic product across two decades.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告比较了二十年的国内生产总值。
senses.why: Each word limits the measure: gross counts everything before allowances, domestic fixes the border, and product names what is made rather than what is earned.
senses.whyCN: 每个词都在限定这个度量：gross 指扣除之前的全部，domestic 固定国境，product 指被做出来的东西而非被赚到的收入。

senses.title: Nominal GDP
senses.definition: output valued at the prices of the year in which it was produced, without removing price change
senses.definitionCN: 按生产当年的价格估值的产出，未剔除价格变动
senses.example: Nominal gross domestic product jumped simply because fuel cost more.
senses.exampleCN: 名义国内生产总值猛增，只是因为燃料更贵了。
senses.why: When current prices are used, a price rise looks like more output, which is why the nominal measure needs a real counterpart.
senses.whyCN: 用当年价格计算时，涨价看起来就像产出增加，因此名义度量需要一个「实际」的对应物。

senses.title: Real GDP
senses.definition: output valued at the prices of a fixed base year, so that only changes in quantity are shown
senses.definitionCN: 按某一固定基年的价格估值的产出，从而只显示数量的变化
senses.example: Real gross domestic product barely moved once inflation was stripped out.
senses.exampleCN: 剔除通胀之后，实际国内生产总值几乎没动。
senses.why: Holding prices constant isolates the physical increase, and the word real here means 'in constant prices', not 'actual'.
senses.whyCN: 把价格固定住就分离出实物的增加，这里的 real 意为「按不变价格」，而不是「真实的」。

senses.title: GDP per head
senses.definition: total output divided by the population, used as a rough measure of average income
senses.definitionCN: 总产出按人口平均分摊，用作平均收入的粗略度量
senses.example: Gross domestic product per capita doubled in a generation.
senses.exampleCN: 人均国内生产总值在一代人的时间里翻了一倍。
senses.why: A total says nothing about how many people share it, so the phrase is routinely divided by population.
senses.whyCN: 总数并不说明有多少人分享它，因此这个短语常被按人口除开。

senses.title: The expenditure measure
senses.definition: the calculation of output by adding household, business, government and foreign spending
senses.definitionCN: 把家庭、企业、政府与国外的支出相加来核算产出的方法
senses.example: The expenditure side of gross domestic product rose with retail sales.
senses.exampleCN: 国内生产总值的支出法一侧随零售额上升。
senses.why: Everything produced is bought by someone, so spending can be added up to reach the same total from the demand side.
senses.whyCN: 被生产出来的东西总会被某人买走，因此从需求一侧把支出加起来也能得到同一个总数。

senses.title: The income measure
senses.definition: the calculation of output by adding wages, profits, rents and other incomes earned in production
senses.definitionCN: 把工资、利润、租金等在生产中获得的收入相加来核算产出的方法
senses.example: The income measure of gross domestic product lagged behind spending.
senses.exampleCN: 国内生产总值的收入法结果落后于支出法。
senses.why: The value of output is paid out as incomes, so the same total can be reached by adding what people earned.
senses.whyCN: 产出的价值会以收入形式发放出去，因此把人们赚到的相加也能得到同一个总数。

senses.title: The output measure
senses.definition: the calculation of output by adding the value each industry contributes, net of intermediate inputs
senses.definitionCN: 把各行业贡献的增加值（扣除中间投入）相加来核算产出的方法
senses.example: The output measure of gross domestic product counts each stage only once.
senses.exampleCN: 国内生产总值的生产法对每一环节只计一次。
senses.why: Counting the same loaf at mill, bakery and shop would inflate the total, so each stage contributes only its own addition.
senses.whyCN: 把同一个面包在磨坊、面包房与店铺各计一次会吹大总数，因此每一环节只计入它自己增加的那部分。

senses.title: The limits of GDP as a welfare measure
senses.definition: the shortcoming that output says nothing about distribution, unpaid work, health or environmental cost
senses.definitionCN: 产出并不说明分配、无偿劳动、健康或环境代价的缺陷
senses.example: Critics say gross domestic product counts the clean-up after a spill as a gain.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者说，国内生产总值把泄漏事故后的清理也算作增益。
senses.why: Because the measure counts market transactions, harm that costs money to repair can appear as growth, which is why the phrase is often invoked to be criticized.
senses.whyCN: 由于这个度量计的是市场交易，需要花钱修复的损害反而会显示为增长，因此这个短语常被拿来作为批评对象。

intro.en: Gross domestic product joins three words: gross, from Old French gros and Late Latin grossus 'thick, coarse'; domestic, from Latin domesticus 'of the house'; and product, from Latin producere 'to lead forth'. The compound term belongs to twentieth-century national accounting. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: gross domestic product 由三个词组成：gross 出自古法语 gros 与晚期拉丁 grossus「厚、粗」；domestic 出自拉丁 domesticus「家的」；product 出自拉丁 producere「引出、产出」。这个复合术语属于 20 世纪国民核算。年代均为约数。

items.en: Grossus meant 'thick, coarse, large'. Source uncertain: its own earlier origin is not established, and Old French gros is the immediate route into English.
items.cn: grossus 意为「厚的、粗糙的、大的」。来源不确定：它更早的来历未得到确认，英语是经古法语 gros 借入的。

items.en: Domus meant 'house, household'; the adjective domesticus 'of the house' supplied English domestic.
items.cn: domus 意为「房屋、家户」；形容词 domesticus「家的」提供了英语 domestic。

items.en: Pro- 'forward' plus ducere 'to lead' gave producere 'to lead forth, to bring out', and so to bring a thing into being.
items.cn: pro-「向前」加 ducere「引导」构成 producere「引出、带出」，因而指把某物造出来。

items.en: Gross entered English in the fourteenth century, domestic in the sixteenth, and product in the fifteenth; each had a life of its own before the phrase existed.
items.cn: gross 于 14 世纪进入英语，domestic 于 16 世纪，product 于 15 世纪；在短语出现之前，每个词都有自己的用法。

items.en: The three words were assembled as one term with the national accounts built in the 1930s and 1940s, when governments needed a single figure for total output.
items.cn: 这三个词是在 20 世纪三四十年代建立国民核算时被组合成一个术语的，当时政府需要一个表示总产出的单一数字。

items.en: The phrase is generally dated to that period, and the abbreviation GDP soon displaced the full form in ordinary reporting.
items.cn: 这个短语一般被认为出自那个时期，缩写 GDP 很快在日常报道中取代了全称。

note.en: The first group holds measures that look almost the same but count different things; the second holds broader names for the size of an economy.
note.cn: 第一组是看起来几乎一样、却计不同东西的度量；第二组是经济规模的更宽泛名称。

entries.definition: Counts output by a country's residents wherever they are, so it includes earnings abroad; the domestic measure counts inside the border.
entries.definitionCN: 按一国居民计算产出，不论他们在哪里，因此包含海外收益；domestic 则只计国境之内。

entries.definition: Subtracts the wearing out of machinery from the gross figure, so it is smaller and closer to sustainable output.
entries.definitionCN: 从总量中扣除机器磨损，因此数值更小，也更接近可持续产出。

entries.definition: Adds up sales at every stage, including intermediate goods, so it double-counts what the product measure counts once.
entries.definitionCN: 把每一环节的销售额都相加，包括中间产品，因此会把 product 只计一次的东西重复计算。

entries.definition: The three initials of the same phrase; in ordinary usage it has largely replaced the full form.
entries.definitionCN: 同一短语的三个首字母；在日常使用中已基本取代全称。

entries.definition: The total earned by residents; it approaches the same figure from incomes rather than from output.
entries.definitionCN: 居民获得的总收入；从收入而非产出接近同一个数字。

entries.definition: The economy's total production, stated without the market-value conventions of the accounts.
entries.definitionCN: 经济体的总产量，不含核算中的市值惯例。

entries.definition: A plain term for what an economy produces; it is not tied to a particular accounting standard.
entries.definitionCN: 经济产出物的日常说法；不绑定某一特定核算标准。

entries.definition: The whole framework of accounts, of which gross domestic product is one headline figure.
entries.definitionCN: 整套核算框架，国内生产总值只是其中的一个头条数字。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: three real words with real roots, a real fixed phrase and a real abbreviation, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：三个有真实词根的词、真实的固定短语与真实缩写，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Read the three words as three limits: gross before deductions, domestic inside the border, product what is made.
normal.cn: 把三个词读成三重限定：gross 是扣除之前，domestic 是国境之内，product 是被造出的东西。

normal.en: The abbreviation takes the initials: G, D and P.
normal.cn: 缩写取三个首字母：G、D 与 P。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: gross domestic product per capita, real gross domestic product, the deflator.
normal.cn: 固定说法：人均国内生产总值、实际国内生产总值、平减指数。

normal.en: Real here means constant prices, not 'true'.
normal.cn: 这里的 real 指不变价格，而不是「真实」。

normal.en: The measure was built with the national accounts of the 1930s and 1940s.
normal.cn: 这个度量是随 20 世纪三四十年代的国民核算建立起来的。

abstract.en: Picture one number standing in for a whole country's year of work.
abstract.cn: 想象一个数字代表整个国家一年的劳作。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger where a spill clean-up is entered on the gain side.
abstract.cn: 想象一本账簿，把泄漏清理记在增益一栏。

abstract.en: Picture a map with a border drawn through it, and only what happens inside is counted.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图中间画着国界，只计界内发生的事。

examples.en: Gross domestic product grew by two percent after adjusting for prices.
examples.cn: 剔除价格因素后，国内生产总值增长百分之二。

examples.en: The country's gross domestic product per capita remains below the regional average.
examples.cn: 该国人均国内生产总值仍低于地区平均水平。

examples.en: Economists use gross domestic product as a rough proxy for the size of an economy.
examples.cn: 经济学家用国内生产总值粗略代表经济规模。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「gross（总的）+ domestic（国内的）+ product（产出）」——国内全部产出加起来 → 国内生产总值

root: gross 出古法语 gros／晚期拉丁 grossus「厚、粗」，更早来源存疑；domestic 出拉丁 domesticus「家的」，源自 domus「家」；product 出拉丁 producere「引出」= pro-「向前」+ ducere「引导」。三者于 20 世纪国民核算中合为一词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one total: everything produced inside a border is added up, and that total is then read at current prices, at constant prices, per head, through spending, through incomes, through industry value and finally as a measure of welfare it cannot be.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个总数展开：国境之内生产的一切被加总，这个总数再依次被读作现价、不变价、人均、支出法、收入法、行业增加值，最后被读作一个它承担不了的福祉度量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a year's ledger spread on a table, every finished thing in the country folded into one figure.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上摊开一年的账本，全国做成的每样东西被折成一个数字。

branches.en: TOTAL AND LIMIT: the same headline figure that sums output also exposes what output cannot say about well-being.
branches.cn: 总数与限度：汇总产出的同一个头条数字，也暴露了产出无法说明福祉的地方。

branches.en: PRICE BASIS: current prices swell with inflation, constant prices isolate quantity.
branches.cn: 价格基准：现价随通胀膨胀，不变价分离出数量。

branches.en: PER HEAD: a total becomes meaningful only when divided among the people who share it.
branches.cn: 人均：总数只有分到分享它的人头上才有意义。

branches.en: SPENDING AND INCOME: the same total can be reached from what buyers spent or what earners received.
branches.cn: 支出与收入：同一个总数可从买方花掉的或挣得者收到的来得到。

branches.en: VALUE ADDED: counting each stage once keeps the total from double-counting the same loaf.
branches.cn: 增加值：每一环节只计一次，避免把同一个面包重复计算。

intro.en: The phrase is three words, each with its own suffix or root, and the pieces also build a large family of English words.
intro.cn: 这个短语由三个词组成，每个词都有自己的词根或后缀，这些成分还构成一大族英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin grossus gives gross and grocer; domus gives domestic, domicile and domain; producere gives product, produce, production and productive.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 grossus 衍生出 gross 与 grocer；domus 衍生出 domestic、domicile 与 domain；producere 衍生出 product、produce、production 与 productive。

items.structure: gross (adjective from Old French gros, Late Latin grossus)
items.example: Gross means the whole before anything is taken away.
items.exampleCN: gross 指扣除任何东西之前的整体。

items.example: The root supplies the 'at home' image behind domestic.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供 domestic 背后「在家中」的意象。

items.example: The adjective gave English domestic.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词给出英语 domestic。

items.meaning: of one's own country; of the home
items.example: Domestic here fixes the measure inside the border.
items.exampleCN: 这里的 domestic 把度量固定在国境之内。

items.meaning: to lead forth; to bring out
items.example: The verb pictures something being brought into being.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把某物被造出来的过程画了出来。

items.example: The noun names what is made, not what is earned.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指被做出的东西，而非被赚到的收入。

items.example: The suffix builds production from produce.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀由 produce 构成 production。

items.example: The suffix builds productive from product.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀由 product 构成 productive。

senses.title: The abbreviation itself
senses.definition: the three-letter short form of gross domestic product, used as a count noun in reporting
senses.definitionCN: gross domestic product 的三字母简写，在报道中作可数名词使用
senses.example: The quarterly GDP figure beat every forecast.
senses.exampleCN: 季度国内生产总值数字超出所有预测。
senses.why: An initialism takes the first letters of a fixed phrase, so the letters carry the whole phrase without repeating it.
senses.whyCN: 首字母缩略取固定短语的首字母，因此这几个字母就承载了整个短语，无须重复全称。

senses.title: The accounting scope
senses.definition: the particular scope of measurement the letters stand for: final output produced inside a border
senses.definitionCN: 这些字母所代表的特定度量范围：国境之内生产的最终产出
senses.example: GDP counts what is made inside the border, not what citizens earn abroad.
senses.exampleCN: GDP 计的是国境之内做出来的东西，而非公民在海外赚到的。
senses.why: Each letter fixes a boundary of the measure, and quoting the abbreviation still commits the speaker to those boundaries.
senses.whyCN: 每个字母都固定了度量的一条边界，引用这个缩写也就意味着接受这些边界。

senses.title: The size of an economy
senses.definition: the total as a shorthand for how large an economy is
senses.definitionCN: 把总数用作经济体有多大的简略说法
senses.example: By GDP the country is the fourth largest in the region.
senses.exampleCN: 按 GDP 计，该国是区域内第四大经济体。
senses.why: A single headline number is convenient for ranking, so the abbreviation comes to stand for size itself.
senses.whyCN: 单一的头条数字便于排名，于是这个缩写转而代表规模本身。

senses.title: Nominal GDP
senses.definition: the total valued at current prices, without adjusting for inflation
senses.definitionCN: 按现价估值、未剔除通胀影响的总量
senses.example: Nominal GDP rose even though output hardly changed.
senses.exampleCN: 名义 GDP 上升了，尽管产出几乎没变。
senses.why: The same headline figure can be computed on two price bases, and the adjective tells the reader which one is meant.
senses.whyCN: 同一个头条数字可以按两种价格基准计算，形容词告诉读者指的是哪一种。

senses.title: Real GDP
senses.definition: the total valued at constant prices, so that only changes in quantity show
senses.definitionCN: 按不变价格估值、从而只显示数量变化的总量
senses.example: Real GDP is the figure analysts compare across years.
senses.exampleCN: 分析人士跨年比较的是实际 GDP。
senses.why: To compare years, price change must be held still, and real marks that adjustment.
senses.whyCN: 要比较不同年份，必须把价格变动固定住，real 标记这一调整。

senses.title: GDP per head
senses.definition: the total divided by population, used as a rough measure of average income
senses.definitionCN: 总量按人口平均分摊，用作平均收入的粗略度量
senses.example: GDP per head says more about living standards than the total does.
senses.exampleCN: 人均 GDP 比总量更能说明生活水平。
senses.why: A larger population can raise the total while leaving each person no better off, so the per-head version is standard.
senses.whyCN: 人口增加可以抬高总量而个人并未变好，因此人均版本是常规做法。

senses.title: The GDP growth rate
senses.definition: the percentage change in the total from one period to the next
senses.definitionCN: 总量从一个时期到下一个时期变化的百分数
senses.example: GDP growth slowed to one percent in the final quarter.
senses.exampleCN: GDP 增长在最后一个季度放缓至百分之一。
senses.why: Because the abbreviation names a quantity, it readily combines with growth to name the change in that quantity.
senses.whyCN: 由于这个缩写指一个数量，它很容易与 growth 组合，指该数量的变化。

senses.title: GDP as a policy target
senses.definition: the total treated as the chief aim of government, often criticized as growth for its own sake
senses.definitionCN: 被当作政府首要目标的总量，常被批评为为增长而增长
senses.example: The plan put GDP ahead of clean water and quiet streets.
senses.exampleCN: 这份规划把 GDP 排在清洁水源与安静街道之前。
senses.why: Once a number is published quarterly, it can be managed as a target, and the abbreviation then names an objective rather than a statistic.
senses.whyCN: 一旦一个数字按季公布，它就能被当作目标来管理，这个缩写于是指一项追求而非一个统计量。

intro.en: GDP is an initialism of gross domestic product: G for gross, D for domestic, P for product. The phrase came together with national accounting in the 1930s and 1940s, and the letters soon became the ordinary name. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: GDP 是 gross domestic product 的首字母缩略：G 代表 gross，D 代表 domestic，P 代表 product。这个短语随 20 世纪三四十年代的国民核算成形，这几个字母很快成为日常名称。年代均为约数。

items.en: G stands for gross, from Old French gros and Late Latin grossus 'thick, coarse, large', meaning the whole before any deduction.
items.cn: G 代表 gross，出自古法语 gros 与晚期拉丁 grossus「厚、粗、大」，意为扣除之前的整体。

items.en: D stands for domestic, from Latin domesticus 'of the house', here meaning what is produced inside the country's own border.
items.cn: D 代表 domestic，出自拉丁 domesticus「家的」，此处指在本国国境之内生产的东西。

items.en: P stands for product, from Latin producere 'to lead forth', naming what is made rather than what is earned.
items.cn: P 代表 product，出自拉丁 producere「引出」，指被造出的东西而非被赚到的收入。

items.en: The full phrase was assembled with the national accounts of the 1930s and 1940s, when a single measure of total output was needed for policy.
items.cn: 全称是在 20 世纪三四十年代建立国民核算时组合起来的，当时政策需要单一的产出的度量。

items.en: The three letters spread through official reports and newspapers in the following decades and largely displaced the full phrase in everyday use.
items.cn: 此后数十年间，这三个字母通过官方报告与报纸传播，在日常使用中基本取代了全称。

items.en: Later combinations such as GDP growth, GDP per capita and GDP deflator show that the abbreviation now behaves like an ordinary noun.
items.cn: 后来的 GDP growth、GDP per capita、GDP deflator 等组合表明，这个缩写如今已像普通名词一样使用。

note.en: The first group holds abbreviations and measures that are constantly confused with GDP; the second holds phrases that name an economy's size in other ways.
note.cn: 第一组是常与 GDP 混淆的缩写与度量；第二组是用其他方式命名经济规模的说法。

entries.definition: Gross national product counts output by a country's residents wherever they are, including income from abroad.
entries.definitionCN: 国民生产总值按一国居民计算产出，不论他们在何处，包含海外收入。

entries.definition: Gross national income measures what residents earn; it is the income-side successor to GNP and not the same as GDP.
entries.definitionCN: 国民总收入衡量居民赚到的收入；是 GNP 的收入侧后继者，与 GDP 不同。

entries.definition: Net domestic product subtracts the depreciation of machinery, so it is smaller than GDP.
entries.definitionCN: 国内生产净值扣除机器折旧，因此小于 GDP。

entries.definition: The phrase the three letters abbreviate; official documents often use it on first mention.
entries.definitionCN: 这三个字母所缩写的全称；官方文件常在首次提及时使用。

entries.definition: What an economy produces, stated without the accounting conventions that GDP carries.
entries.definitionCN: 经济体生产出的东西，不带 GDP 所含的核算惯例。

entries.definition: Total incomes earned by residents; it approaches the same total from the other direction.
entries.definitionCN: 居民获得的总收入；从另一方向接近同一个总数。

entries.definition: A loose way of speaking about how large an economy is, for which GDP is the usual yardstick.
entries.definitionCN: 谈论经济体有多大的宽松说法，GDP 是其常用尺子。

entries.definition: The system of production and exchange itself; GDP is one number about it, not the thing itself.
entries.definitionCN: 生产与交换的系统本身；GDP 只是关于它的一个数字，而非它本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the three initials, the full phrase behind them and real fixed compounds, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：三个首字母、其背后的全称与真实的固定组合，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: G for gross, D for domestic, P for product: three letters, three limits.
normal.cn: G 是 gross，D 是 domestic，P 是 product：三个字母，三重限定。

normal.en: The full form is gross domestic product; the letters simply take its initials.
normal.cn: 全称是 gross domestic product；这几个字母只是取其首字母。

normal.en: Fixed compounds: GDP growth, GDP per capita, GDP deflator, real GDP.
normal.cn: 固定组合：GDP growth、GDP per capita、GDP deflator、real GDP。

normal.en: Real GDP means constant prices; nominal GDP means current prices.
normal.cn: real GDP 指不变价格；nominal GDP 指现价。

normal.en: The measure belongs to the national accounts of the 1930s and 1940s.
normal.cn: 这个度量属于 20 世纪三四十年代的国民核算。

abstract.en: Picture a number flashing on a screen before anyone has read the report behind it.
abstract.cn: 想象屏幕上一个数字先跳出来，背后的报告还没人读过。

abstract.en: Picture a country's whole year compressed into one line of a table.
abstract.cn: 想象整个国家的一年被压成表格里的一行。

abstract.en: Picture a border drawn on a map, with only what happens inside counted.
abstract.cn: 想象地图上画着国界，只计界内发生的事。

examples.en: GDP rose by two percent in the year after the new port opened.
examples.cn: 新港口启用后的一年里，GDP 上升了百分之二。

examples.en: Comparisons of GDP across countries depend on how prices are converted.
examples.cn: 跨国比较 GDP 取决于价格如何换算。

examples.en: The government was accused of chasing GDP while ignoring the rivers.
examples.cn: 政府被指责一味追逐 GDP 而无视河流的状况。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「G（总）+ D（国内）+ P（产出）」——三个首字母合成一个国家的年度成绩单 → 国内生产总值

root: GDP 为 gross domestic product 的首字母缩略；gross 出古法语 gros／晚期拉丁 grossus（厚、粗，更早来源存疑），domestic 出拉丁 domesticus（domus 家），product 出拉丁 producere（pro- 向前 + ducere 引导）。缩略用法随 20 世纪国民核算普及。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one abbreviation: the three letters stand for a measured total, and that total is read as a scope, a size, a price basis, a share per head, a rate and finally a policy aim.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个缩写展开：三个字母代表一个被度量的总数，这个总数再依次被读作核算范围、经济规模、价格基准、人均份额、一个比率，最后是一项政策目标。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a number flashing on a press-room screen, taken as the country's report card for the year.
core.cn: 核心意象：发布厅屏幕上一个跳出的数字，被当作这个国家一年的成绩单。

branches.en: LETTERS AND SCOPE: the initials carry a phrase, and the phrase fixes what is counted and where.
branches.cn: 字母与范围：首字母承载一个短语，而短语固定了计什么、计哪里。

branches.en: SIZE AND CURRENT PRICES: a headline total ranks economies, and at current prices it swells with inflation.
branches.cn: 规模与现价：头条总数给经济体排名，而按现价它会随通胀膨胀。

branches.en: CONSTANT PRICES AND PER HEAD: the total is adjusted for price change and then divided among people.
branches.cn: 不变价与人均：总数先按价格变动调整，再分到人头上。

branches.en: RATE: the same total becomes a percentage change from one period to the next.
branches.cn: 比率：同一个总数变成相邻时期变化的百分数。

branches.en: AIM: a published statistic turns into something a government is expected to deliver.
branches.cn: 目标：一个公布的统计量变成政府被要求交付的东西。

intro.en: This entry is an initialism, so its parts are three letters rather than prefixes and suffixes; the letters in turn stand for words with their own roots.
intro.cn: 这一条是首字母缩略，因此它的构成是三个字母，而不是前缀与后缀；这三个字母又分别代表有自己词根的词。

latinIntro.en: The letters abbreviate gross, domestic and product, whose roots are Late Latin grossus, Latin domus and Latin producere; the abbreviation itself has no Latin form.
latinIntro.cn: 这三个字母缩写的是 gross、domestic 与 product，其词根分别为晚期拉丁 grossus、拉丁 domus 与拉丁 producere；缩写本身没有拉丁形式。

items.example: The letter carries the first limit of the measure.
items.exampleCN: 这个字母承载度量的第一重限定。

items.example: The letter fixes the border of the count.
items.exampleCN: 这个字母固定计数的边界。

items.example: The letter names the thing measured.
items.exampleCN: 这个字母命名被度量的对象。

items.example: Gross output is counted before wear and tear.
items.exampleCN: 总产出在磨损扣除之前计算。

items.example: Domestic output excludes what is made abroad.
items.exampleCN: 国内产出不含在国外制造的东西。

items.example: The product measure counts final goods only.
items.exampleCN: 产出度量只计最终商品。

items.example: The suffix marks the adjective of the house.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀标记「家的」这一形容词。

items.meaning: the short name of the measure
items.example: The initialism behaves like an ordinary noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个首字母缩略像普通名词一样使用。
